meta.contract_name: Magic Strategy Engine Contract — Rule Registry
meta.purpose: Machine-readable registry of every documented rule the execution engine must cite. The objective of this contract is FIDELITY, NOT PROFIT: it exists so that (a) every automated decision can cite the documented rule that produced it, (b) the engine can emit telemetry proving what it detected and which rules fired, and (c) conformance to the documented strategy can be tested from that telemetry alone.

meta.id_policy: STABLE. Rule ids are the citation tokens the engine embeds in its decision records. They MUST NOT be renumbered, reused or repurposed across contract versions. A rule that is withdrawn is marked status=WITHDRAWN and kept; a rule that is superseded points at its successor. New rules take the next free number in their family.

field_semantics.status: One of the five values in meta.status_vocabulary, which is the single authority: READY = Implementable and testable as written. · OPEN = Blocked on a decision the trader declined to give. NEVER invent a value. · CALIBRATED = Fitted to the trader's own annotated charts, not stated by him. Carries proxy/n. Never presented as doctrine. · WITHDRAWN = Rule retired — the object it described has no basis in the corpus. · DEFECT = (now empty) Source self-contradiction. All 8 cleared by the corpus triage with zero trader input. — merged in v1.2.1. This field previously defined only READY / OPEN / DEFECT while three rules use CALIBRATED or WITHDRAWN, so a validator reading this block would have rejected its own file.

authority_class.documentary: Traces to a workspace page (000–213) or a chart screenshot. §1–§9.
authority_class.R: Trader ruling. Authoritative; beats the workspace where they conflict.
authority_class.O: Trader ruling that switches OFF something the workspace or the images actively teach. The dead rule stays visible.
authority_class.D: Numeric machinery invented for the engine. Present in no workspace page and none of the 1,258 images. NEVER doctrine, never quotable as strategy.
authority_class.A: Prior AI assistant commentary inside the ruling document. ZERO strategy authority; recorded only so its numeric proposals are traceable.

field_semantics.banned_inputs: Input classes the trader explicitly prohibited. A conformance test asserts none of these appears in the rule's decision record.

verification_label.label: UNVERIFIABLE_HERE
verification_label.meaning: The cited material was never redistributed to this repository, so the citation was not checked and COULD NOT HAVE BEEN. Distinct from UNVERIFIED, which implies we tried and failed. The remedy is to request the corpus, NOT to file a defect.
verification_label.why_a_third_label: The adjudication package contradicts itself: its CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 says an unfollowable citation must be treated as UNVERIFIED, while SOURCE_INDEX.md item 2 says DO NOT treat an uncheckable citation as unverified doctrine. Both are right about different things — hard rule 2 guards against assuming a ruling whose evidence we COULD have checked and did not; SOURCE_INDEX guards against dismissing a ruling because the author did not redistribute his primary material, which at 84% would make the package unusable. Ruling: UNVERIFIABLE_HERE for structurally-absent material, UNVERIFIED (hard rule 2) for anything checkable we have not checked.

rules.name: Heavy Disturbance Hard Skip
rules.statement: If disturbance_grade == HEAVY, the engine MUST NOT open a trade — regardless of Structure Box grade, momentum state, amplifier count, or any alignment score. risk_pct is forced to 0. There is no override path. Verbatim: “Heavy Disturbance is a hard filter: no trade regardless of the Structure Box.”
rules.inputs: disturbance_grade from GATE-002, computed on the alignment layout at the execution timeframe; structure_box_grade (does not affect the outcome — record it for telemetry so conformance can prove the gate fired before sizing).
rules.output: decision = BLOCK; block_reason = HEAVY_DISTURBANCE; risk_pct = 0.0; disturbed_asset_list recorded.
rules.notes: Do NOT implement the softer wordings that exist for the same rule — Q7 p.18 “the trade should usually be skipped”, and F5/027/022's “i will 90% skip the trade”. An engine cannot implement “usually” or “90%”. Q14 is the latest and most explicit and wins; the three statements must not be quoted interchangeably (§10.F.1 defect D6b).

rules.name: Disturbance Count Classifier
rules.statement: Count the correlated assets in the layout that are 'disturbed'. 0 disturbed → NONE. Exactly 1 → LIGHT. 2 or more → HEAVY (“or the market no longer exhibits a coherent directional alignment”). An asset is disturbed when “it is no longer supporting the expected trade direction while the majority of correlated assets still are”, per any of the trader's six named off-conditions: (1) order flow opposite to what the correlation implies; (2) fails the expected MSB/BOS while others confirmed; (3) moving toward a completely different liquidity objective; (4) reacts significantly before or after the others; (5) different momentum profile; (6) creates a structural reversal while others trend.
rules.inputs: Per-correlate structural read at the execution TF (same TF as the main asset, GATE-007): order-flow direction, MSB/BOS state, current liquidity objective, LEVEL-STATE comparison of objective progress across assets (has this asset swept or reached its objective while the others have not, or did it react before reaching it — NOT relative timing, NOT a clock, round-2 OFF_4), momentum profile, structural-reversal flag.
rules.output: disturbance_grade ∈ {NONE, LIGHT, HEAVY}; per-asset state; which off-condition fired for each disturbed asset (required telemetry).
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q9, pp.20–21); drawn correlates at §9.F IM36 — 0281 shows ONE offending pane = Light, 0287 shows TWO = Heavy
rules.notes: This is the first hard boundary anywhere in the corpus. The drawn six of IM36 are compatible but NOT identical: the PDF adds “different momentum profile” and “creates a structural reversal” and drops IM36's “never swept LIQ before MSB”. Neither list is declared exhaustive — keep both. The two lists are ONE PREDICATE WITH TWO ENUMERATIONS: every drawn slide in both families closes “It causes DISTURBANCE (Reduce the RISK)”. Keep both. The CAUSES axis is OPEN — his framing is a sampler (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:79 “all kinds of possible examples”, :85 “what else can we talk about”, :91 “here's another idea”) and the governing rule is a DEFINITION at 065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:83 — “if the correlated asset do not act the way they are supposed to act i call it magic disturbance”. The SEVERITY axis IS CLOSED and stated: none / light / heavy. OFF_4 IS NOW IMPLEMENTABLE and comes off NOT_EVALUATED: lead/lag is a LEVEL STATE to him, never a clock — “having reaction before sweeping the close liquidity” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:85), “already swept the liquidity but other assets are still trying to reach the liquidity” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:89), “most Altcoins lag, they will have open targets to clear” (066_Magic_Quadrant_For_Altcoins.md:9). NEGATIVE CASE, to prevent false positives: being further along the MSB->BOS sequence is explicitly NOT a disturbance — “it is fine it makes no difference for me” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:19). Uses no correlation coefficient, no candle count and no clock, so it complies with his own bans. OFF_5 (different momentum profile) STAYS NOT_EVALUATED — it depends on the un-fittable momentum-regime boundary. [ENGINEERING] to pin: the shared evaluation instant, and what counts as swept/cleared (wick touch vs close-through) applied identically to every asset. DO NOT gate detectors behind a “majority of other panels aligned” precondition: on a 3-correlate roster with 2 disturbed it suppresses both detections, drops the grade from HEAVY to NONE, and sizes a full-risk trade in a market the trader would skip. Canonical grade reference images: 053_untitled.md's “Capture d'écran 2024-02-02 22xxxx/23xxxx” series (§9.K IM119).

rules.name: Disturbance count does not normalise to layout size
rules.statement: The '≥2 → HEAVY' threshold is an ABSOLUTE count stated without reference to how many correlates the layout holds. 2-of-2 (the IM31 Essential layout) = 100% disagreement and is sensible; 2-of-3 (the fixed BTC layout) grades HEAVY; but §2 F1/106 permits five positive and five negative correlates and calls that layout STRONGER — 2-of-10 would also grade HEAVY and the trade would be skipped, penalising exactly the layout the workspace calls stronger. The engine MUST NOT silently substitute a ratio threshold. Interim requirement: freeze the layout to the four-panel BTC roster (GATE-008) so 2-of-3 is the only heavy case, and log layout_size with every disturbance grade so the eventual ruling can be applied retroactively to stored telemetry.
rules.inputs: layout_size (COUNT OF PANELS — the main asset plus its correlates; pinned round 2, [ENGINEERING], so the four-panel BTC roster is 4, not 3), disturbed_count
rules.output: telemetry fields layout_size and disturbed_count alongside every disturbance_grade.
rules.citation: §2 F5 ⚠ caveat; §10.F.1 defect D5b; §10.C disturbance-counts row (PDF Q9, pp.20–21)
rules.notes: RESOLVED round 2: the roster is FROZEN to the four-panel layout; the absolute >=2 threshold stands; the engine REFUSES TO GRADE if the layout differs; and layout_size and disturbed_count are emitted with every grade so an eventual ratio ruling can be applied retroactively to stored telemetry. THE UNIT COLLISION IS RESOLVED BY DECLARATION: `inputs` previously said “layout_size (count of correlates)” while the triage text said “refuse to grade at all if layout_size != 4” (panels) — two different units, one name. PINNED HERE to PANELS, i.e. the main asset plus its correlates, so the four-panel BTC roster (BTCUSDT.P + USDT.D + TOTAL + ETHUSDT.P) has layout_size = 4 and the conformance assertion must agree. [ENGINEERING] — this is our declaration, not his; he froze nothing.

rules.name: Does the MAIN asset count toward the disturbance count?
rules.statement: RULED: the main asset is NOT scored for disturbance. Q7's directional score includes BTC; Q9 says “Each CORRELATED asset receives one of three states”. A main asset that disagrees with its own setup is not a disturbance — it is an ABSENT SETUP, and must stop the evaluation upstream via main_asset_state = SETUP_INVALID rather than being counted toward the >=2 HEAVY threshold. The engine records main_asset_counted as a declared parameter on every evaluation.
rules.inputs: main_asset_state; correlate_states
rules.output: telemetry flag main_asset_counted: bool
rules.notes: TWO COUNTS OVER TWO DIFFERENT SETS. ALIGNMENT includes the main panel — his own handwritten note card “PERFECT MAGIC ALIGNMENT! / 4 MSB + 4 BPR = 4 Assets ALIGNED! / ZERO DISTURBANCE!” on a 4-panel BTCUSDT.P + USDT.D/TOTAL/ETHUSDT.P screenshot (images/Putting_All_Together/0443_05509bb4.png). DISTURBANCE is tagged on correlates only: the main pane is never tagged across the drawn slides (images/Questionnaire/0280-0287, images/Magic_Alignment_Setup/). SHIPS AS INFERENCE, NOT AS HIS RULE — the corpus prints no explicit exemption sentence, so main_asset_counted is a DECLARED PARAMETER carrying authority=ENGINEERING and ratified=false in `values`, never a bare doctrine value. THE COMPENSATING GATE IS REQUIRED AND DOES NOT YET EXIST: emit main_asset_state = SETUP_INVALID as a hard upstream skip that never reaches grading. NOT OPTIONAL — exclusion alone lowers disturbed_count, lightens the grade and RAISES the risk cell, so it is a systematic tilt toward LARGER positions rather than a neutral gap. STATE OF PLAY, recorded rather than smoothed over: MAIN_ASSET_COUNTS=False has been live in shadow since commit fd52295 on 2026-08-08 (gate_002_disturbance.py:356, wired at evaluator.py:351), so the exclusion has run WITHOUT its gate. main_asset_state was added to TELEMETRY_SCHEMA.json by T-0027 but is NOT yet in setup_evaluation.required, because no producer computes the verdict; SETUP_INVALID is emitted by nothing. THIS ROW IS NOT SETTLED until the gate exists — tracked in KNOWN_ISSUES.md. rules.name: Disturbance must be STRUCTURAL, never statistical (ban list)
rules.statement: The engine MUST NOT determine disturbance from correlation coefficients, a fixed number of candles, or a time delay. “The strategy evaluates structural agreement, not statistical correlation.” Explicitly banned engine rules, verbatim: “The correlation dropped below 0.75” · “The asset must confirm within two candles” · “The MSB must occur within five minutes”. A conformance test asserts that the stored disturbance decision record cites only structural facts and contains none of these input classes.
rules.inputs: n/a — a negative constraint on the implementation, testable from the disturbance decision record alone.
rules.output: conformance assertion pass/fail
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q9, pp.20–21); §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER
rules.notes: The parallel ban for fake-MSB detection is at PDF Q10 p.24: no “reversal within N candles”, no maximum candle count, no fixed time delay — “implementation shortcuts rather than trading concepts”.

rules.name: The ±80% correlation figure is asset-SELECTION only, never a live gate
rules.statement: The ±80% correlation rule chooses WHICH assets belong in the layout. It is not the trade-confirmation metric. The engine MUST NOT compute a rolling correlation coefficient as a trade filter and MUST NOT reject or downgrade a setup because a measured correlation fell. Trade confirmation is live structural agreement, order-flow agreement, momentum agreement and target agreement.
rules.inputs: layout roster (static configuration), not a live price series.
rules.output: conformance assertion: no correlation coefficient appears in any accept/reject decision record. Testable via rule_evaluation.banned_input_check plus the key regex of HG-03.
rules.citation: §2 F2 [R] (PDF Q7, p.18); §9.F IM31 — the slides print “-80% NEGATIVE CORRELATED ASSET” / “+80% POSITIVE CORRELATED ASSET” without saying whether they are measured live; the trader rules they are not
rules.notes: The banned_inputs list is what makes this negative gate testable: without enumerated tokens the `output` is a conformance assertion with nothing to assert against, and telemetry's `rule_evaluation.banned_input_check` — the only mechanism in the schema for proving a negative — cannot be applied. 0.75 is named explicitly because §7.4 records it as a number the trader raised in order to kill it. banned_inputs added in v1.1.0: as originally written this rule declared a conformance assertion with no enumerated tokens, so the schema's banned_input_check mechanism — the only machinery that makes a negative gate testable — could not be applied to it.

rules.name: Alignment timeframe MUST equal execution timeframe
rules.statement: “All assets must be checked on the same timeframe when confirming the entry.” That timeframe is the execution timeframe. A confirmation assembled from mixed timeframes across the layout is a violation. The particular member of the set is hedged three times in the source (“usually”, “such as”, “sometimes 30-minute”) — the SAME-TF requirement is the hard part, not the specific 5M/15M/30M list.
rules.inputs: execution_tf; each layout asset's series at that same tf.
rules.output: conformance assertion; telemetry alignment_tf (must equal signal_tf).
rules.citation: §2 F1 [R]; §10.C BTC-layout-roster row (PDF Q7, p.16); §9.F IM33 — Screen 1's sync config is Symbol OFF / Interval ON, i.e. one TF across all panes

rules.name: BTC layout roster fixed by name (four panels)
rules.statement: For BTC trading the layout is exactly four panels — main: BTC · positive: ETH and TOTAL · negative: USDT.D. Expected order flow for a BTC long: BTC, ETH, TOTAL bullish and USDT.D bearish; for a BTC short, the mirror. There is no panel called “total dominance”. Canonical tickers: BTCUSDT.P (Binance), ETHUSDT.P (Binance), TOTAL (CryptoCap), USDT.D (CryptoCap).
rules.inputs: instrument = BTC
rules.output: layout roster + expected_sign per asset (used by GATE-002 to decide 'supporting the expected trade direction').
rules.citation: §2 F1 [R], §2 I2 [R] (PDF Q7, p.16); §9 IM38 (ticker composition table and the seven-symbol watchlist); §9.F IM31/IM33
rules.notes: Left unruled: whether the engine trades altcoins at all, and the entire `Risk Altcoin` column of 053 (9 of its 18 cells unaddressed). Altcoins cannot be magic-aligned at all — “we can not rely on any kind of magic alignments when we trade Altcoins” (066) — so GATE-001/002 have no defined behaviour for them (§10.F.2 item 13).

rules.name: Alignment MUST NOT require same-candle simultaneity
rules.statement: The engine MUST NOT require all assets to print the exact same structure at the exact same candle — “That would be too rigid.” Magic alignment exists when the main asset, positive correlates and negative correlates show COMPATIBLE ORDER FLOW around the entry area. Six admissible agreement forms, any of which satisfies the gate: (a) all assets MSB in the same entry window; (b) some already MSB'd and now continuing with BOS; (c) one leads / one lags but still moves toward the same idea; (d) positives not fighting the main asset; (e) the negative moving opposite as expected; (f) similar target logic (liquidity, imbalance, key levels, institutional levels). Banned as a confirmation metric, verbatim: “the last BOS on the 15-minute chart matches on all assets”.
rules.inputs: Per-asset order flow and structure state at the execution TF within the entry window.
rules.output: alignment_form — which of the six fired (required telemetry, so conformance can prove the engine did not apply a stricter test than documented).
rules.citation: §2 F1 [R] (PDF Q7, pp.15–17); §9.F IM34 — the printed maxim “Remember! MSB or BoS is NOT the KEY! TREND is the KEY! Trending in the same direction!”; §7.4
rules.notes: “Entry window” is never bounded numerically anywhere in the corpus, and any candle-count or minute bound would collide with GATE-005's ban.

rules.name: Magic alignment confirmation is a REQUIRED entry criterion
rules.statement: A valid entry requires all five canonical criteria: Liquidity · Imbalances (primary POI) · Market Structure & Momentum · Forward/Reverse trading context · Magic Alignment confirmation. Magic Amplifiers are optional. An order opened with no alignment read recorded is a conformance failure regardless of outcome.
rules.inputs: The five criteria evaluations for the candidate setup.
rules.output: entry_criteria_record (five booleans + evidence), plus amplifiers_present.
rules.notes: Not settled by the ruling: E15 “Location Over Setup”, the super-BPR > BPR > imbalance sub-ranking of the primary POI, and the slides that draw the entry AT the block (§10.F.2 item 17).

rules.name: Two competing alignment scorers — the count rule must win
rules.statement: Two mutually inconsistent scorers exist for the same decision. (a) The disturbance COUNT rule (0 / exactly 1 / ≥2) is the one wired to the 9-cell risk matrix. (b) The [D] Magic Alignment Score 0–100 proposes bands “80–100 Strong · 50–79 Light disturbance / reduced risk · Below 50 Heavy disturbance / skip trade” over seven listed considerations with NO component weights — so it is not implementable as written — and it can disagree with the count (3 aligned + 1 disturbed is LIGHT by count but could fall below 50 here, depending on weights that do not exist). The engine MUST NOT implement the 0–100 bands as a gate. The count rule should win because it is the one wired to the risk numbers — but the PDF never says so, and Q7 presents its own bands as the risk gate.
rules.inputs: disturbance_grade (GATE-002)
rules.output: risk gate driven by the count rule; any 0–100 score, if computed at all, is telemetry only and may not affect accept/reject.
rules.notes: The Magic Alignment Score is class [D] — invented engine machinery present in no workspace page and none of the 1,258 images, never traded. Never cite it as strategy.
rules.triage_note: NOT ADJUDICATED in the corpus-triage pass — listed explicitly so silence is not mistaken for resolution.

rules.name: News blackout — 15 minutes BEFORE a red-folder event
rules.statement: No new trade may be OPENED within 15 minutes before the scheduled time of any high-impact (red-folder) economic event on the calendar for the traded instrument's currency set. The rule addresses new entries only; it says nothing about positions already open.
rules.inputs: Economic calendar (Forex Factory / Crypto Craft) filtered to red folders; event scheduled time in NEW YORK local time; current NY time; instrument currency set (GATE-015).
rules.output: decision = BLOCK; block_reason = NEWS_PRE_WINDOW; event_id and event_time recorded.
rules.citation: §1.8 [R]; §2 G5 [R]; §10.C news-blackout-before row (PDF Q12, p.27)
rules.notes: The 15 / 30 / M15 constants appear in NO workspace page and in NONE of the 1,258 images — they are trader-authorised engine constants, not recovered doctrine, and the trader ships them while explicitly saying “The strategy does not use a fixed number of minutes… For implementation purposes, use the following deterministic rule” (§10.C, §7.4).

rules.name: News blackout — 30 minutes AFTER, then the first COMPLETE M15 close
rules.statement: No new trades for at least 30 minutes after the scheduled release. After the 30-minute cooldown, the engine must ADDITIONALLY wait for the first complete M15 candle to close before allowing new entries. Both conditions must hold; the M15 close is an extra condition, not a substitute for the 30 minutes. “The objective is not to trade the news, but to avoid the manipulation immediately surrounding the release.”
rules.inputs: Event scheduled time (NY); the M15 series on the traded instrument; current NY time.
rules.output: first_permitted_entry_time = max(release + 30min, close of the first M15 candle that completes at or after release + 30min); BLOCK until then with reason NEWS_POST_WINDOW.
rules.citation: §2 G5 [R]; §1.8 [R]; §10.C news-blackout-after row (PDF Q12, p.27)

rules.name: Exceptional-event indefinite disable — resumption condition undefined
rules.statement: For exceptional events — FOMC, emergency central-bank announcements, major geopolitical events, exchange failures such as FTX — trading REMAINS DISABLED until volatility has clearly normalized, “even if this exceeds the standard 30-minute window”. The event CLASS is enumerable from the two image tables. The RESUMPTION CONDITION is not: “volatility has clearly normalized”, “abnormal volatility (large impulsive candles or wide ranges)” and “normal market structure” are all undefined, and the same document elsewhere forbids exactly the statistical shortcuts an implementer would reach for. The engine MUST NOT invent a numeric volatility test; it must expose the resumption decision as an explicit, logged state transition.
rules.inputs: News feed classified against the event taxonomy; a volatility/structure read whose criterion is undefined.
rules.output: BLOCK with reason NEWS_EXCEPTIONAL; a resumption event that records who/what authorised it.
rules.citation: §2 G5 [R]; §10.F.2 item 24 (PDF Q12, p.27). Event taxonomies: §9.H IM44 — VERY HIGH: inflation (CPI, PPI, Core CPI, Core PPI), interest rates (Federal Funds Rate, Main Referencing Rate, Official Bank Rate), employment (Unemployment Claims, Job Openings, Non-Farm Employment Change, Unemployment Rates), growth (GDP), statements (FOMC talks/statements/conferences/projections, Monetary Policy Statements and Reports); HIGH: all PMI, Industrial Production, Capacity Utilization. §9.H IM45 — VERY HIGH: elections/referendums, bankruptcies, pandemics, scandals (FTX), lawsuits (Binance), war or coup, political decisions (a government banning Bitcoin); HIGH: big innovations, long recessions, natural disasters

rules.name: Red-folder calendar scope and timezone contract
rules.statement: The calendar filter is Forex Factory RED FOLDERS ONLY — “the highest impactful data… growth, inflation, employment, central bank, business surveys and speeches for the currencies”. Currency selection: for FX, the traded pair's own currencies; for crypto, “USD is enough however for extra confluence i can use EUR, GBP and USD”. The calendar's timezone must be set to New York local so calendar timestamps and chart timestamps match.
rules.inputs: Calendar feed; instrument → currency set mapping; calendar timezone setting.
rules.output: The event list that GATE-012/013/014 consume.
rules.citation: §2 K1 (001_Economic_Data_for_Morning_Routine.md); §3.0 step 1; §9.H IM44; §2 G1 (001: “my Forex Factory timeframe is also set to UTC-4 New York local time so they are matching”)

rules.name: Whole-DAY eco-data avoidance vs the minutes window — unreconciled
rules.statement: The workspace gate is a DAY-level gate; the engine constant is a MINUTES-level gate, and nothing reconciles them. Workspace: “Trading before economic data should be avoided at all costs. There will be manipulation after manipulation, fake market structure shifts, fake BOS, fake liquidity hunts… Economic data days are the times when people blow their accounts”; “smart money is disturbed here, it does not work as they are supposed to be, this is why we avoid trading eco data days or at least use extremely small cash”; eco-data days are named as the first cause of setups “destined to fail”. Engine: −15 min / +30 min / first M15 close. An implementer must be told whether a red-folder day is tradeable at all outside the ±window, and whether risk is reduced on such days.
rules.inputs: is_red_folder_day (calendar); risk_pct from the matrix.
rules.output: Undefined until ruled — record is_red_folder_day on every trade so the two readings can be tested against outcomes.
rules.citation: §1.8 (001, 084); §2 G5; §2 H17 (056); §3.7 step 5 (“Reduce/skip on eco-data or global-event days”); §10.C
rules.notes: 001 carries a nuance pointing toward the minutes reading — day traders “only avoid the first volatility and use the volatility later on” and “never trade the outcome” — but it never states that the day itself is then tradeable.

rules.name: Execution on LTF only — no trade may be opened from an HTF
rules.statement: The higher timeframes (Monthly, Weekly, Daily, 4H, 2H, 1H) are ANALYSIS ONLY: “No trades are opened from these timeframes.” The lower timeframes are used exclusively for trade execution and “do not redefine the higher-timeframe destination unless the higher-timeframe strategic analysis itself changes”. Any order whose triggering signal was detected on an HTF series is a violation, testable from telemetry.
rules.inputs: signal_tf recorded on every trigger; the HTF destination (analysis output) held constant across LTF events.
rules.output: conformance assertion signal_tf ∈ execution_set; telemetry signal_tf and analysis_tf recorded separately on every trade.
rules.notes: Corroborating ruling: “An MSB alone should never invalidate a higher-timeframe directional bias” (PDF Q10, pp.23–24).

rules.name: The execution-timeframe set excludes documented execution timeframes
rules.statement: The trader's set is “{30M, 15M, 5M} … used EXCLUSIVELY for trade execution”. But the workspace executes on 1M and 3M: “even though we observe the 1H concerning liquidity our entire trade setup is based on the 1Min chart” (086), “an entry around this 3Min BB” (111), and a live “1Min MSB” / “1Min market structure shift” (062, 104). Separately, 022 puts 30M on the SWING side (“day trading = TFs UNDER 30Min”) while the ruling makes 30M an EXECUTION timeframe. The document does not say whether the trader narrowed his set or the list is incomplete, and flags neither shift as a change. Do not silently admit or exclude 1M/3M.
rules.inputs: candidate signal_tf
rules.output: Undefined until ruled; record signal_tf on every trade regardless.
rules.citation: §3.3 [R] ⚠; §10.C execution-timeframes row; §10.F.1 defect D11; §10.F.2 item 23 (PDF Q1, p.3; Q13, p.28)
rules.triage_note: HARD legal set {30M,15M,5M}; ANY tf below 5M (3M, 2M, 1M all observed in the corpus) is a FLAGGED EXTENSION emitting LTF_BELOW_RULED_SET.

rules.name: Day-trading mode only — the swing branch is switched OFF
rules.statement: 022 Step 2's daily swing-vs-day-trade checkbox is removed for the engine: “The strategy is a day-trading strategy… The engine should therefore operate in day-trading mode, not swing mode. HTFs = Analysis only. LTFs = Execution only.” Consequence for this slice: the session/timing gates are now UNCONDITIONAL — the “only when day trading / swing traders don't need sessions” qualifier that 022 attached to the 08:30–11:30 window no longer has a false branch.
rules.inputs: n/a — a mode constant.
rules.output: mode = DAY_TRADE (fixed); no user-selectable style.
rules.notes: Also removes the risk of reading the 2024 journal's HTF picture packs as swing evidence: “The 2024 journal is not a swing-trading journal… making it a day-trading workflow” (PDF Q13, p.28).

rules.name: NY Magic Zone 08:30–11:30 — preferred, never stated as exclusive
rules.statement: The preferred execution window is 08:30–11:30 New York time: “The best time zone to trade is from 8:30AM to 11:30AM New York local TF this is the 3 hours time trading range magic zone for day traders” — 08:30 news volatility, 09:30 the US stock open “injects an extreme amount of volume”, and “after 11:30AM… markets generally slow down… as day traders we need extreme volatility”. Confirmed verbatim as the engine's preferred window. BUT “preferred” is not “only”: whether entries are legal between 11:30 and 19:00 is never stated, while the exit rule keeps positions alive until 19:00 NY. Implement as a SOFT gate that FLAGS out-of-window entries rather than blocking them, until the trader rules.
rules.inputs: current NY local time; mode = DAY_TRADE (GATE-019).
rules.output: in_magic_zone: bool; flag OUT_OF_PREFERRED_WINDOW on any entry outside it (a deviation record, not a failure).
rules.citation: §2 G3 (022_Magic_Strategy_Plan.md) + [R]; §10.C preferred-execution-window row; §10.F.2 item 20 (PDF Q13, p.28)

rules.name: 09:30 NY Open entry clustering
rules.statement: The author's own stated primary entry timing: “If you're a day trader or scalper, your best entry areas generally happen around the 9:30AM New York open” (105); “around the New York open you can find your great entry timing” (100); “I'd rather mostly focus on 9:30AM New York opening rather than all other sessions” (059). Reversal shifts are repeatedly narrated at 9:30 the next morning (104). Record every entry's offset from 09:30 NY so the learning loop can test whether the engine's fills cluster where the trader's do.
rules.inputs: entry timestamp (NY)
rules.output: telemetry minutes_from_NYO (signed).
rules.citation: §2 G4 (105, 100, 111, 104, 113, 059); worked cases 086, 089; §4.1 (the reverse-trade-from-institutional-sweep setup is anchored at 9:30 NYO)
rules.notes: The PDF never mentions 09:30 at all — the omission is recorded at §10.F.2 item 20. This is documented preference, not a ruling, hence SOFT.

rules.name: 19:00 NY hard session close
rules.statement: Any position still open at 19:00 New York time is closed. This is the terminal condition of the v1 exit model: 70% of the position at 2R, the remaining 30% runs “until either: the final target is reached, the stop-loss is hit, or the end of the trading session (19:00 New York time), at which point any remaining position is closed”.
rules.inputs: NY clock (DST-aware); open position state.
rules.output: forced flatten at 19:00 NY; exit_reason = SESSION_CLOSE.
rules.citation: §2 H12 [O]; §2 G7 [O]; §3.6 [O]; §10.C session-hard-close row (PDF C2, pp.29–30)
rules.notes: NOT OPEN. The trader ruled it in his own first-person register for the live system (answers C2: “an alternative discretionary trade management technique that I use manually”; “We can always add the ladder exit later”). Ships HARD_GATE. PROVENANCE, recorded rather than hidden: every 19:00 in his 213 Notion pages belongs to one 2023 EURUSD program — 046_untitled.md:8, 047_untitled.md:8 (duplicate), 138_untitled.md:6/11/29, 144_untitled.md:6/11/29, including a literal “19:00 stop” column, 26 rows, EURUSD and NZDUSD, pip-denominated. ZERO crypto pages mention it. His method contains no exit-timing step; 036_Single_Trade_Management.md is empty (title only). COUNTER-INSTANCE: images/Examples/1197_663b46b1.png + 1198_64a1e91d.png — BTCUSDT.P 1m, New York axis (header “Oct 11, 2023 03:53 UTC-4”), mid-day entry, his annotated 27000 “AMPLIFIED TARGET” reached ~22:30 NY; a 19:00 flatten cuts it ~3.5h early. This is going back to him with the two charts, so implement the flatten AND log would_have_been_flattened_at_1900 and time_in_trade on every trade, so a reversal applies retroactively to stored telemetry. Fires on ANY remaining position, partial taken or not. Resolve 19:00 DST-aware from the tz database, never a fixed offset. Also unstated and NOT implied: whether new entries are barred before 19:00. Default: not barred, and flag.

rules.name: Time base is New York local (DST-aware, not a fixed UTC offset)
rules.statement: All timestamps — chart, calendar, session windows, the news blackout windows, the Magic Zone and the 19:00 close — are New York local time. The workspace states UTC-4 twice (“my trading we timeframe is set to UTC-4, basically New York local time”, 001; also 059) and UTC-5 once (“New York local TF which is currently UTC-5”, 033). The PDF uses “New York time” as the invariant throughout and never states an offset. Implement with an America/New_York timezone, not a hardcoded offset — otherwise every window in this slice shifts by an hour twice a year.
rules.inputs: system clock; tz database
rules.output: All gate evaluations timestamped in NY local; the offset used recorded in telemetry.

rules.name: Session windows (level marking, not entry permission)
rules.statement: Session ranges supply liquidity levels, not entry permissions: “each session creates its own ranges… once a session completed its TF, you know now where the high liquidity resides at the high and low of the ranges”. Indicator windows: Asia 20:00–00:00 NY, London 02:00–05:00 NY, drawn as backgrounds + name labels only and visible on ≤15Min charts. Hunt sequence: Asia range set → Asia high/low used as fuel during London → structure carries toward the daily target.
rules.inputs: NY clock; intraday series
rules.output: session_high / session_low levels available to the liquidity layer; NOT a gate on entry legality.
rules.notes: The Asia END time is unresolved — 033's own wording is “my Asia Setting is set to 20:00PM to noon”, almost certainly a slip for midnight; the real value lives only in the settings screenshot (§7.1.11). CHART_ANALYSIS/SYNTHESIS §5.1 reports the indicator dialog itself reads 20:00 — 00:00 (Technical_Indicators/0373), which settles it from the images, not from the trader.

rules.name: 2R reward floor — reject any stop candidate below 2R
rules.statement: For each stop-loss candidate, compute the resulting Risk:Reward using the PREDEFINED trade target. “If the RR is below 2R, reject that stop-loss and evaluate the next tighter option.” “2R is the minimum acceptable reward.” Preference hierarchy for telemetry: Preferred ≈3R · Acceptable 2R–4R · Poor below 2R · “Overly Tight” significantly above 4R (e.g. 8R–10R). The engine must NOT optimise for the highest possible RR — “it should optimize for the best balance between market protection and reward potential”.
rules.inputs: entry price; target price (fixed BEFORE stop selection); the price of each of the five stop anchors from GATE-027.
rules.output: Full candidate table [{anchor, stop_price, rr, accepted}] — required telemetry, since conformance is tested from it.
rules.citation: §2 H5 [R]; §2 H9 [R]; §3.5 step 2; §10.C reward-floor row (PDF Q11, pp.25–26)
rules.notes: This hardens 023 Step 8's question (“Which SL level gives you a 1:3 risk/reward ratio?”) into a rejection threshold. Documentary corroboration: the worked ladder at 026/075 rejects the deepest-structure stop precisely because it yields 1:1 — “not a great trade” — then accepts the imbalance stop at 2R (“a 1:2 ratio is a great start”) and calls the 3R liquidity stop “optimal”. Also 027/074/076: “If a trade setup is giving you 1:1 ratio, skip it do not bother at all, all your money will be gone to fees and commissions”, and H6's fee argument, “the real risk reward ratio is actually less than what you expected… this is why you shall never aim less than 1:2 ratios”.

rules.name: No candidate reaches 2R → NO TRADE
rules.statement: If every stop candidate on the five-anchor ladder produces RR < 2R against the predefined target, no trade is taken. This is a terminal skip — it is not licence to move the target, widen the reward, or re-anchor the stop outside the five categories.
rules.inputs: The candidate table from GATE-025.
rules.output: decision = BLOCK; block_reason = NO_CANDIDATE_REACHES_2R; the full rejected table retained.
rules.citation: §2 H9 [R]; §3.5 (PDF Q11, p.26). The explicit “If no candidate reaches 2R, no trade should be taken” sentence appears in the prior-assistant restatement at §10.E A-5 — the trader's own step 2 supplies the rejection and his ladder supplies the exhaustion

rules.name: Stop-candidate ladder — the five anchors in engine order
rules.statement: Evaluate stop-loss candidates in exactly this order: 1. Deepest Swing (deepest LL/HH) · 2. Momentum Imbalance · 3. Previous Liquidity Sweep / Quasimodo · 4. Order Block · 5. Inner MSB. “This order reflects the natural preference of the strategy. The first options provide more room for natural pullbacks, while the later options progressively reduce that cushion.” It is cushion-monotonic. The engine MUST use this order — the workspace's printed order (§2 H8, §3.5, §8), which runs Order Block THIRD and hunted-liquidity/QML fourth, is superseded for execution.
rules.inputs: Chart objects at the entry location: deepest LL/HH after the MSB; the deeper open momentum imbalance; the swept wick / SFP tip / PDL-sweep extreme; the OB high/low; the inner MSB (plus any residual imbalance to cover).
rules.output: Ordered candidate list feeding GATE-025.
rules.citation: §2 H8 [O]; §3.5 step 1 [O]; §8 SL-placement menu; §10.B O5 (PDF Q11, p.25)
rules.notes: RESOLVED round 2. (a) Anchor #3 is a SWEPT LIQUIDITY LEVEL — swept prior swing / SFP tip / PDL-sweep level. The trader removed the QML requirement himself: “it does not have to be QML, any old liquidity sweep level can act as SL level for me, i do not have perfect standards for this” (026_Stop_Loss_Decision.md:46, dup 075_Stop_Loss_Decision.md:46). SHIP NO QML DETECTOR. Rung 3 is locatable and the skip licence is withdrawn from TELEMETRY_SCHEMA.json. Exact placement of the stop on the level is [ENGINEERING] — declare it. (b) The wide-cover case is a ZONE-COVERAGE MODIFIER APPLIED AFTER ANCHOR SELECTION, not a sixth anchor: if the chosen stop lands inside a zone object, extend to the far edge of the whole zone (075 Choice 4; 049_Examples.md:5; 116_Examples.md:5; PRIM-006, zones never lines). Residual [ENGINEERING]: the snap tolerance for the adjacent-but-not-intersecting case, and whether the widening runs before or after the 2R floor and before sizing. The pictorial ranking of candidates is drawn at §9.J IM63 (“Most Ideal / Second most Ideal / Least Ideal”, the tightest annotated “Stopped Out Already”).
rules.triage_note: Round-2 P2: this row uniquely lacked the resolution and triage_note fields its neighbours GATE-028 and GATE-029 received in the same pass. Both sub-items are now ruled; the residuals are [ENGINEERING] placement questions, not doctrine gaps.

rules.name: DEFECT — “largest stop whose R:R is closest to 3R” is self-contradictory
rules.statement: BLOCKER. PDF Q11 step 4 reads: “select the largest (most cushioned) stop-loss that still provides an acceptable reward, with preference given to values closest to 3R”. Risk:Reward falls MONOTONICALLY as the stop widens, so among survivors the LARGEST stop always has the LOWEST RR — nearest 2R, never nearest 3R. On the PDF's own worked table (Deepest Swing 1R → rejected · Momentum Imbalance 2R accept · Liquidity Sweep/QML 3R selected · Order Block 4R “valid but tighter” · Inner MSB 10R “valid but excessively tight”), “largest ≥2R” selects the 2R Momentum Imbalance while “closest to 3R” selects the 3R Liquidity Sweep — TWO DIFFERENT STOPS and two different position sizes. The PDF answers Liquidity Sweep, so its own example is decided by the “closest to 3R” clause and the word “largest” is dead text. Do not ship either reading silently. Operative rule as actually applied, pending a trader ruling: among candidates with RR ≥ 2R, select the one whose RR is CLOSEST TO 3R; break ties toward the larger (more cushioned) stop.
rules.inputs: Surviving candidates from GATE-025.
rules.output: selected_stop; selection_rule_id — MUST be logged so conformance can test which reading actually shipped, and so the learning loop can attribute outcomes to the reading.
rules.citation: §2 H9 ⚠; §3.5 step 2; §8 SL-placement menu; §10.F.1 defect D1b (PDF Q11, pp.25–26). Provenance of the “closest to 3R” wording: §10.E A-5 — it originates in the prior AI assistant's rewrite of the developer's proposal (“your developer”, “your course”, “your philosophy”), which materially changed the developer's largest-first-with-3R-tiebreak rule while claiming only to remove ambiguity — plus the trader's own step 4
rules.triage_note: Selector = argmin |RR - 3.0| over candidates with RR >= 2.0; ties to the larger stop. 'Largest' is DEAD TEXT.

rules.name: No upper R:R rejection cut — a 10R stop passes as written
rules.statement: The Preference Hierarchy leaves 4R < RR < 8R UNNAMED, “significantly above 4R” is not a threshold, and “Overly Tight” is a LABEL, not a rejection — the PDF's own table calls the 10R Inner MSB “Valid but excessively tight”. So if the only candidate clearing 2R is a 10R stop, the algorithm AS WRITTEN takes it — directly against the strategy's own philosophy and against the cushion preference (“i personally take larger SLs more than tighter SLs, if i am not forced”, 075; “Extremely tight stop-losses are not automatically better simply because they produce higher RR”, Q11). No maximum-RR skip rule is given anywhere. The engine must either expose a configurable upper cut (and log it) or flag every selection above 4R.
rules.inputs: selected_stop.rr
rules.output: flag RR_ABOVE_ACCEPTABLE_BAND when rr > 4.0; block only if a cut is later ruled.

rules.name: Prefer the larger cushion stop
rules.statement: “Prefer larger cushion stop losses whenever possible. Only move to tighter stop-losses when the reward becomes insufficient.” Documentary form: “A large SL will give you a lot space for the price to pull back… you will not be easily stopped out, you can cut the trades earlier and get out with BE”; tight SL: “no room for a pullback… you'll be instantly stopped out”. Default: “i personally take larger SLs more than tighter SLs, if i am not forced”. A tighter-than-necessary selection is a FLAG with a recorded reason, not a failure.
rules.inputs: Candidate table; selected_stop.
rules.output: flag TIGHTER_THAN_NECESSARY + reason when a tighter candidate is chosen over a wider one that also cleared 2R.
rules.citation: §2 H7 [R] (PDF Q11, pp.25–26); 026_Stop_Loss_Decision.md / 075_Stop_Loss_Decision.md; the pictorial argument at §9.J IM63 — three candidate stops ranked “Most Ideal / Second most Ideal / Least Ideal”, the tightest annotated “Stopped Out Already” on the same chart as the trade that worked

rules.name: DEFECT — a 2R-exact setup makes the 30% runner degenerate
rules.statement: The default exit banks 70% at 2R, while GATE-025 accepts ANY candidate with RR ≥ 2R against the predefined target. When the selected stop yields exactly 2R the partial level IS the final target: 70% closes there, “the final target is reached” fires, and the 30% runner never runs. No minimum gap between partial level and final target is stated, and it is never said whether a 2R-only setup should be taken at all given the runner adds nothing.
rules.inputs: selected_stop.rr; partial_level (2R); target price.
rules.output: flag DEGENERATE_RUNNER when selected_stop.rr ≤ 2.0 + ε; the engine must not silently invent a minimum gap.
rules.citation: §2 H12 ⚠; §10.F.1 defect D10b (PDF C2, pp.29–30 read against Q11, pp.25–26)
rules.notes: Compounding gap: “the active trade management rules” that govern the 30% runner are NEVER DEFINED — “the single most load-bearing undefined phrase in the document” — and the only workspace page bearing that name (036_Single_Trade_Management.md) is empty (§10.F.2 item 21, §10.F.3).

rules.name: The authoritative 9-cell risk matrix (lookup table)
rules.statement: risk_pct = LOOKUP(structure_box_grade, disturbance_grade). Manipulated: No 1.50% · Light 0.75% · Heavy 0% (skip). Super: No 1.25% · Light 0.50% · Heavy 0% (skip). Standard: No 1.00% · Light 0.25% · Heavy 0% (skip). As stored in 053_untitled.md's `Risk Alignment` column in decimals: 0.015 / 0.0075 / 0 · 0.0125 / 0.005 / 0 · 0.01 / 0.0025 / 0. Source of truth: “let's use the latest 'Risk % Setups' database as the source of truth”. The 076 prose tier (Manipulated 2% / Super 1.5% / Standard 1%) is DEAD for the engine, as are H2's 2% ceiling and §9.G IM40's “2% = 2R reserved for a 4R Perfect setup” pairing — both become unreachable cells, retired by omission and never explained.
rules.inputs: structure_box_grade ∈ {Standard, Super, Manipulated} (box-grading key: pullback taps gap only = Standard; sweep of inner low + gap tap = Super; sweep + gap tap + fake MSB trapping both sides = Manipulated); disturbance_grade from GATE-002.
rules.output: risk_pct; then position quantity via the RR tool's Qty against the virtual account size.
rules.citation: §2 H3 [O]; §3.7 step 3; §10.A.1; §10.B O3 (PDF Q9, p.21; Q14, p.29); cross-checked cell-by-cell against 053_untitled.md; box-grading key at §8 and §2 A8/A9/A10 (057, 063, 105)

values.exact_relation: LIGHT = NONE - 0.0075 (0.75 percentage points), exact for all three grades

rules.notes: The PDF defines the Manipulated box WITHOUT the imbalance/gap tap (Q10: sweep + counter-trend MSB + both sides trapped + continuation) and never defines Standard or Super at all, despite making them the table's key. Since the box grade drives the risk %, an engine built only from Q10 will mis-grade boxes — keep the workspace key (§10.F.2 item 15).

rules.name: DEFECT — the “base risk × 0.5” modifier double-sizes the most common grade
rules.statement: BLOCKER. The proposed refactor — Base Risk (Manipulated 1.50% / Super 1.25% / Standard 1.00%) × Disturbance modifier (No ×1 · Light ×0.5 · Heavy ×0) — claims “This produces exactly the same results as the table”. IT DOES NOT. Manipulated 1.50 × 0.5 = 0.75% matches. Super 1.25 × 0.5 = 0.625% vs the table's 0.50% (+0.125 pp, 25% more risk). Standard 1.00 × 0.5 = 0.50% vs the table's 0.25% — EXACTLY DOUBLE; on a $100,000 account a Standard box with light disturbance sizes at $500 instead of $250, and Standard is the most common grade. Keep the LOOKUP TABLE. The true relationship is SUBTRACTIVE and exact for all three grades: Light = No − 0.75 percentage points (1.50−0.75=0.75; 1.25−0.75=0.50; 1.00−0.75=0.25). Equivalently, per-box multipliers ×0.50 / ×0.40 / ×0.25 — not a single ×0.5. Equivalently again, in units of 0.25%: No = {6,5,4}, Light = {3,2,1}, Heavy = {0,0,0}. Most economical description: the Light row is numerically identical to 053's own `Risk Altcoin` column (0.0075 / 0.005 / 0.0025). The ×1 and ×0 legs are correct; only the ×0.5 leg is wrong.
rules.inputs: structure_box_grade; disturbance_grade
rules.output: conformance assertion: the shipped sizer must reproduce all nine cells exactly; a single multiplicative modifier cannot express the table.
rules.notes: Attribution is AMBIGUOUS, leaning prior-assistant (“One suggestion from my side:” … “I'm happy to keep the lookup table if it's simpler for implementation”). Either way it is engine machinery, not doctrine, and it is arithmetically wrong. The defect is DOWNSTREAM-ONLY: both printed source tables are verified clean — the 9-cell matrix reproduces 053's Risk Alignment column cell for cell, and §9 IM30's CASE table is verified correct exactly as printed. An engine that reads the tables verbatim is safe; only the “cleaner” restatement is not.
rules.triage_note: Ship the literal 3x3 lookup from 053_untitled.md. DELETE the 'x disturbance modifier' path entirely — it double-sizes the most common grade.

rules.name: DEFECT — the momentum “Bullet Train” band 15–20 is unreachable
rules.statement: BLOCKER. The 8-component Momentum Score's printed per-component maxima are +3, +3, +3, +2, 0, +3, 0, 0 → MAX = +14; the minima are 0, 0, 0, 0, −2, 0, −4, −5 → MIN = −11. TRUE REACHABLE RANGE = [−11, +14]. The printed bands are “15–20 Bullet Train · 11–14 Strong · 7–10 Moderate · 3–6 Weak · ≤2 Exhausted”, so the single best market state the engine can ever observe scores 14 and is graded merely “Strong”. Shortfall: 1 point to enter the band at all, 6 points to reach its stated ceiling of 20. This BREAKS THREE OTHER RULINGS that gate on the bullet-train state: Q1 p.2 (Step 3 context validation, “Momentum strength (bullet-train vs. slowing market)”), Q2 p.4 (“Continue if: Momentum remains strong ('bullet train')”) and Q6 p.15 (“This commonly occurs during bullet-train momentum”). Do not silently pick a fix — either the positive components are missing 6 points, or the bands must be re-cut against a +14 ceiling, and the document gives no basis to choose. The bands are otherwise contiguous and non-overlapping, and ≤2 correctly absorbs the whole negative range down to −11.
rules.inputs: The eight components: Structure Writing (+3/+2/+1/0) · Momentum Imbalance Quality (+3/+2/+1/0) · Impulse Candle Quality (+3/+2/+1/0) · Imbalance Respect (+2/+1/0) · Counter-Imbalance Obstacles (0/−1/−2) · Structure Box Quality (+3 Manipulated / +2 Super / +1 Standard / 0 none) · Trend Weakness (0/−2/−4) · Reverse Signals (0/−3/−5).
rules.output: Any gate that consumes 'bullet train' must be marked unimplementable until ruled; log the raw score and the band assigned.
rules.citation: §10.D D-2; §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER; §2 D6 [R] ⚠ (PDF Q5, pp.8–11)
rules.notes: The whole Momentum Score is class [D] — invented engine machinery appearing in no workspace page and in none of the 1,258 images, never traded; never quote it to a trader as “the method”. The NAME “Bullet Train” is genuine workspace doctrine (023, 062) and is unaffected — only the machinery that would assign it is broken. Component 6 is additionally a coupling nothing in the workspace makes: the same three-grade structure-box scale that sets RISK % now also feeds a MOMENTUM number, and the PDF never says which box is meant (entry box or box at the destination).
rules.triage_note: WITHDRAWN: the Momentum Score is invented engine machinery with ZERO corpus instances. Do not re-band, do not add 6 points. Superseded by GRADE-032 (already READY).

rules.name: Momentum must be read structurally — banned input classes
rules.statement: Momentum “is not defined by candle body size, ATR ratios, or a fixed number of impulsive candles… momentum is a structural concept that evaluates the quality of the journey toward the selected liquidity or imbalance target”. Impulse candles “increase confidence, but structure and liquidity remain the primary drivers”. Banned as inputs to ANY gate in this slice: ATR ratios / “Y × ATR”; “retrace ≥ 60%” as a deep-V definition; fixed distance/percentage tests for concerning liquidity — “The engine should not ask: 'Is liquidity within X% or Y × ATR?'”; and the assistant-authored imbalance tiers 0.8% / 0.4–0.8% / <0.4%, which were proposed and disowned in the same sentence.
rules.inputs: n/a — a negative constraint testable from the decision record.
rules.output: conformance assertion: no banned input class appears in any gate evaluation.
rules.citation: §2 D1 [R]; §2 D3 [R]; §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER; §10.E A-3 (PDF Q5, pp.7–9, 12; Q1, pp.1, 3; Q3, pp.5–6)

rules.name: The engine MUST be able to output NO TRADE (stand-aside)
rules.statement: The workspace has an explicit stand-aside state; the engine procedure as specified does not. Documentary: “price is right in the middle of PDH and PDL, then nothing is your concern at the moment” (089); §9.B IM14 “Future Interest” — “price is far away from both LIQ LEVELS… As a scalper I cannot carry price to UP 1H LIQ or DOWN 1H LIQ points far far away”; 023 Step 1 “if far → not my concern for the moment”, Step 2 “if far, wait”; 024's mid-way case = “no certain bias here”. Q1's three-step procedure ALWAYS yields “the next unresolved objective” and has no stand-aside output — “The engine as specified cannot output 'no trade'.” A stand-aside output is mandatory; the condition that TRIGGERS it is deliberately unfixed, because the trader bans fixed % and ATR distance tests (GATE-035).
rules.inputs: Distance/relationship of price to the nearest concerning objectives above and below; the active bias.
rules.output: decision = STAND_ASIDE with a recorded reason — must be a first-class outcome, not the absence of a signal.
rules.citation: §2 B18 (089_Examples.md); §9.B IM14; §3.1a ⚠; §1.7 (024_Liquidity_Clash_of_Titans.md); §10.F.2 item 1
rules.open_half_note: Ships the descend-until-actionable procedure; the leaf 'concerning' test is CALIBRATED-pending, ban-free reachability first.

rules.name: Premium/discount and OTE MUST NOT gate a trade
rules.statement: Negative gate. “The bot should not use a premium/discount (equilibrium or OTE) entry filter. Although I understand the concepts, they are not part of my entry criteria… The engine should therefore ignore premium/discount or OTE as an entry condition… it should not influence whether a trade is taken or rejected. It is neither a required confirmation nor a filtering criterion.” The geometry survives as READING VOCABULARY only. Conformance test: no accept/reject decision record may cite premium, discount, equilibrium, or OTE.
rules.inputs: n/a — a negative constraint on the decision record.
rules.output: conformance assertion pass/fail, evaluated via rule_evaluation.banned_input_check and the HG-16 key regex. The geometry may be RECORDED (primitives.ranges) as reading vocabulary; it may never appear on an accept/reject path.
rules.citation: §3.4 [O]; §6 glossary rows PREMIUM/DISCOUNT/DEMAND and OTE/ROTE; §10.B O7 (PDF C3, p.30)
rules.notes: “The single biggest image-vs-trader override in the corpus” — the images teach it as live doctrine: §9.J IM116 (the 0.5 split on the author's own charts), IM64–IM68 (entries sited by half — SUPER BPR 8H in the discount half for a long, LTF SUPER BPR in the premium half for a short), IM57 (an entry built on the 0.7–0.8 OTE strip), IM107 (an OTE OZONE entry), and 105 lists “premium and discount” among the things used at entry. A vision layer will keep detecting it; it must never reach the gate. banned_inputs added in v1.1.0 for the same reason as GATE-006: a negative HARD gate needs enumerated tokens or its assertion has nothing to assert over.

rules.name: Amplifiers MUST NOT create a trade
rules.statement: Negative gate. “Amplifiers never create a trade by themselves. They only increase the confidence of an already valid setup. A valid trade is always based on market structure, liquidity, imbalance, momentum, and forward/reverse trading logic.” COLLISION TEST, for confidence scoring only, ruled round 2 as an INTERVAL INTERSECTION: a level-type amplifier collides when zone_low <= amp_price <= zone_high; an area-type amplifier collides on any interval overlap. No percentage is consulted on this primary test. A secondary “or very close to” branch is [ENGINEERING] — see values.amplifier_edge_tolerance_pct, measured from the zone's NEAREST EDGE. All amplifier types are weighted equally: institutional key levels (PDH, PDL, PWH, PWL, PMH, PML, DO, WO, EQ), round numbers, S/R flip areas, and any future types.
rules.inputs: entry POI price; amplifier level prices.
rules.output: amplifier_count and types (telemetry / confidence only) — MUST NOT flip an accept/reject decision.
rules.citation: §2 E16 [R]; §3.4 item 5 [R]; §10.C amplifier-collision row (PDF Q8, p.19); 067_Magic_Amplifiers.md
rules.notes: RESOLVED round 2 — the three-bases question DISSOLVES. His own material never states any distance: 067_Magic_Amplifiers.md is the complete lesson and its only proximity formulation is “colliding or very close to my entry area” (067_Magic_Amplifiers.md:46); no percentage appears in any of the 213 pages or in any of the 16 amplifier images. His DRAWINGS define collision as an interval intersection: in images/Magic_Amplifiers/0813_6b653ec8.png the AMP line runs through the interior of the dashed “POI ENTRY AREA” box (note card “All we care the COLLISION!”); in images/Magic_Amplifiers/0817_3baffc72.png the amplifier is a band fully CONTAINING the POI box. PRIMARY TEST: interval intersection, no percentage. SECONDARY [ENGINEERING] BRANCH: tolerance from the zone's NEAREST EDGE, not its centre — amplifier_edge_tolerance_pct, default 0.2, declared and stamped. AUTHORITY: the 0.2%, the 99.80/100.20 worked example and the “closer to the center of the entry zone” weighting exist ONLY in answers Q8, which is IMPERSONAL SPEC PROSE rather than the trader's voice, and which self-labels the number “an engineering guideline, not a strict market rule”. COMPARISON FORM: band, inclusive — lo = anchor*(1-pct), hi = anchor*(1+pct), lo <= amp <= hi. The subtraction form abs(amp-anchor) <= 0.002*anchor fails the spec's own worked example at BOTH endpoints in float64 (0.20000000000000284 > 0.2), with < or <=. NON-DECISIONAL: output is telemetry/confidence only and MUST NOT flip an accept/reject decision, so none of this can change a trade. LARGER OPEN ITEM, now carried in the schema: every amplifier is modelled as a scalar price, but S/R flips are ZONES (PRIM-006); zone-vs-zone overlap had no representation — see TELEMETRY_SCHEMA.json amplifier.geometry / zone_low / zone_high / collision_test. Volume Profile HVN remains silently dropped from the PDF's amplifier list while it claims to treat “all” amplifiers equally (§10.F.2 item 16, unruled).

rules.name: Do not fade a bullet train (heavy-momentum stand-aside)
rules.statement: Documented preference with no automatable trigger. “Can you stop a train that is coming at you at 300Km/H with a i-MSB or 1Min MSB?… you will need a cooling of a consolidation period to reverse the movement and probably HTF MSBs like 5Min or 15Min” (062). “Price is like a bullet, like thunder hitting you, if i see 1Min market structure shift here i will be hesitant i cannot trust this trade” (104). “Taking a trade against such a momentum is quite dangerous… instead trading a setup with a slow momentum is so much easier and smooth because the price was already cooling off” (061). Before fading, run the diagnostic checklist: missed a deeper concerning area? deeper liquidity? unchecked timeframes? missed institutional levels or candlesticks? an economic data release? a global event (war etc.)? — “Momentum does not appear randomly, there is always something happening that you are missing” (062).
rules.inputs: Momentum state at the concerning area; the six-item diagnostic checklist.
rules.output: flag COUNTER_MOMENTUM_ENTRY + the checklist result.
rules.citation: §2 D6 (023_Questionnaire.md, 062_Momentum.md, 104_Examples.md); §2 D8 (061); §8 momentum picture
rules.notes: The gate is real doctrine but the MACHINERY that would assign 'bullet train' is broken — see GATE-034. Cannot be automated as specified.
rules.open_half_note: Ships the mandatory six-item checklist; the counter-momentum permission half is unresolved.

rules.name: Cool-off is a hard prerequisite for a reverse trade; ambiguity resolves to CONTINUE
rules.statement: A sweep alone never authorises a reversal: “still after the sweep, it has no intention to reverse, there's no failing imbalance or structure shift, it needs a cool off period, a slow down in momentum before considering a reversal” (100). Observed durations in the workspace: “the momentum slowdown takes around 2 days before the reversal” (100) and “it takes around 24H to cool off until it totally loses its momentum, then the price shifts at 9:30AM in the morning the next day” (104). FAILURE-SAFE DIRECTION: if the structural confirmations are not present, “the engine should assume that the liquidity sweep was only part of the ongoing trend” — ambiguity resolves to FORWARD/CONTINUE, never to Reverse. And “An MSB alone should never invalidate a higher-timeframe directional bias.”
rules.inputs: Time and structure since the sweep; the seven confirmation conditions (GATE-041); the HTF directional bias.
rules.output: mode ∈ {FORWARD, REVERSE}, defaulting to FORWARD; cool_off_elapsed recorded.
rules.notes: RESOLVED round 2 — TWO DIFFERENT LISTS SHARE ONE PHRASE, which is what produced the alleged contradiction. “Price slows down after reaching the destination” is the FIRST of the Q6 SEVEN (answers Q6) and is ALIVE: c1_price_slows is a required telemetry boolean, asserted by K-13/K-27. What cool-off (D7) is absent from is the Q5 FIVE “named transition conditions” (answers Q5: score drops · imbalance failures appear · opposite imbalances form · failed imbalances flip to S/R · opposite structure writes) AND the Momentum Score's components — and the Momentum Score is WITHDRAWN regardless. Dropped from the score: yes. From the Q6 seven: no. From the decision: no. SCOPE: this is a MODE-LAYER gate. Output is a direction defaulting to FORWARD (K-12 scopes the assertion to direction_mode == “REVERSE”). It gates the Forward->Reverse transition and NEVER BLOCKS A FORWARD SETUP — blocking forward setups costs real trades. DURATION: cool_off_min_hours = null. It is a STRUCTURAL test with no time term; emit elapsed_hours as evidence rather than gating on it. Exactly two durations exist in the corpus, both narrated observations on single dated frames — 100_Examples.md:21 (~2 days) and 104_Examples.md:11 (~24H); “the next morning” is the tail of the 24H sentence, NOT a third data point. The PDF does not retire the durations, it OMITS them, so they stand unopposed as the only quantities the corpus has.

rules.name: “Multiple structural confirmations” for Forward→Reverse is unquantified
rules.statement: The switch to Reverse requires “multiple structural confirmations” drawn from seven: price slows down after reaching the destination · momentum begins deteriorating · momentum-imbalance failures appear · new momentum imbalances form in the opposite direction · failed imbalances become S/R flips · those new opposite-direction imbalances successfully hold price · a valid micro Market Structure Break (MSB) confirms the new direction. HOW MANY of the seven, and whether any is mandatory (e.g. the micro MSB), is never stated. Absent them the default is CONTINUE (GATE-040). Related unquantified gate: “Has the Momentum Score deteriorated enough to justify a reversal?” has no absolute score, no delta and no lookback window.
rules.inputs: The seven condition evaluations at the destination.
rules.output: confirmations_present (list) + the threshold actually applied — the threshold must be logged, since it is a choice not a rule.
rules.open_half_note: Ships the conservative conjunction default; quorum_ratified=false until the trader confirms.

rules.name: All-TOTALs-cleared stop-trading protocol (crypto)
rules.statement: If TOTAL, TOTAL 2 and TOTAL 3 all clear their higher-timeframe targets, stop trading: “ONE QUESTION! What if all TOTALS clear their TARGETS in High Time Frames?” → “ANSWER: Close your TRADES! And Take profit from SPOT INVESTMENTS! Great times to stop trading and watch the price! Possible MARKET CRASH or Possible SHORT Positions!” Text form: “great times to stop trading and watch the price because there is a possible market crush or possible short positions”.

The source wording is emphatic ('Close your TRADES!') but the trigger — all three TOTALs 'clearing their targets' — depends on target-selection, which is itself OPEN. A rule resting on an unresolved input cannot be a hard gate.

rules.name: Strike-losses circuit breaker
rules.statement: “What do i do in Case of Strike Losses? — Stop Trading — Don't look at the Charts for a Week — Analyse what really happend — Ease back into it slowly.” “Strike losses” is never quantified anywhere in the corpus — no consecutive-loss count, no drawdown percentage, no time basis.
