rules.output: flag CIRCUIT_BREAKER_CANDIDATE — cannot be automated until a threshold is supplied.
rules.citation: §2 H16 (009_Technical_Concepts.md); §3.6 (“Circuit breaker: strike losses → stop trading a week, analyse, ease back”)

rules.name: Range validity by exact-EQ construction
rules.statement: Object-validity gate for the vision layer. In this corpus the EQ / `0.5` midline is EXACT BY CONSTRUCTION: measured at the exact arithmetic midpoint of the two boundaries to within ≤1 px on EVERY split-range frame across four families, the sole exception being 0163 at 2.75 px (a drafting slip); the census closed at twenty-two frames. Therefore: COMPUTE EQ from the boundaries — never read the drawn line — and treat a midline that misses the arithmetic midpoint as evidence the object is NOT one of this deck's ranges. Worked confirmation on a frame from outside the Range families: CASE 010's unlabelled overlapping red-upper/green-lower pair measures x 476→817, top border y 167, base border y 274, midline y ≈219.5 against an arithmetic midpoint of 220.5 — exact to 1 px, i.e. within border width — which is what settles it as a premium/discount split rather than a BPR overlap.
rules.inputs: Detected range boundaries (high, low) and, on annotated-frame ingestion only, any drawn midline. Evaluated ONLY when the engine emits a range object (telemetry primitives.ranges); otherwise NOT_APPLICABLE.
rules.output: is_valid_range: bool; computed_eq (from the boundaries, never read off); eq_source; midline_error_px (annotated frames only, null on live charts).
rules.citation: §8 measurement discipline; §9.J IM93, IM101, IM116; §9 IM30 (CASE 010 measurement)
rules.notes: Scope clarified in v1.1.0. The live-enforceable half is 'compute EQ from the boundaries, never read the drawn line' (eq_source must be COMPUTED_FROM_BOUNDARIES). The ≤1 px census bound is CORPUS CALIBRATION over the annotated screenshot deck and cannot be evaluated against live market data, where no drawn midline exists — midline_error_px is null there. Before v1.1.0 this rule had no telemetry surface at all and CONFORMANCE_SUITE HG-38 asserted over fields that existed in no record.
rules.runtime_assertion: ALWAYS testable on live data: computed_eq MUST equal the arithmetic midpoint of the two range boundaries, and eq_source MUST be 'computed'. An engine that reads a drawn midline instead of deriving it is non-conformant regardless of market data.
rules.corpus_only: midline_error_px and the 22-frame census are calibration over ANNOTATED screenshots and are null on live charts. That half is ADVISORY and must not produce a FAIL.
rules.team_lead_note: Adjudicated AGAINST a blanket downgrade. The critic flagged this as HARD_GATE-but-unenforceable; that is true only of the px census. The instruction 'compute EQ from the boundaries, never read the drawn line' is enforceable on every live record, and violating it is a real conformance failure. Enforceability stays HARD_GATE, scoped to the runtime half.

rules.name: Position-bracket vs retracement-tool discriminator
rules.statement: Chart-recognition validity gate. A TradingView position tool's risk fill and reward fill occupy the SAME column range and meet on one bright-green entry rail (a confirmed rail colour is RGB(4,223,15) on 0183). Two boxes that share a PRICE BAND but differ in TIME are an S/R flip drawn twice, never a bracket. FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS: the 0/0.5/1 retracement tool — 0194 and 0196 each carry the full bracket signature and neither is a position tool. Discriminator: ordinal labels (`0`/`0.5`/`1`) PLUS an exactly 1:1 split — measured midpoint error 0.005 and 0.085 USDT. A position tool's legs are UNEQUAL (this deck's are ~1 : 2.9); a retracement tool's are equal to a rounding error. Also: absence of a heavy in-plot entry rail does NOT rule out a position tool when matching axis tags are present — confirm each level TWICE, against a box edge AND its own axis tag, pairing red (stop) with green (entry) tags.
rules.inputs: Detected coloured fills, their x-spans, shared boundaries, axis tags, and any ordinal labels.
rules.output: object_class ∈ {POSITION_TOOL, RETRACEMENT_TOOL, SR_FLIP, OTHER} + the evidence used.
rules.citation: §8 measurement discipline (a discipline that has already overturned four codex claims — IM69/0073, IM89 scope, IM110/0189, IM114/0201)

rules.name: ≈2.9 house R:R and its structurally explained exceptions
rules.statement: Family-identification rule, not a trading rule. ≈2.9 : 1 is the deck's HOUSE reward-to-risk wherever a bracket is ILLUSTRATIVE rather than a specific trade. All ten CASE cards measured: 0208 2.85 · 0209 2.89 · 0210 2.90 · 0211 2.87 · 0212 2.89 · 0213 2.87 · 0214 2.88 · 0215 2.93 · 0216 2.92 · 0217 2.87 — 0216 is the series' only short (red risk box ABOVE green reward) and still measures 2.92, so the ratio survives the direction flip. Range-Bias illustration cards: 0173 = 2.93 (six brackets, spread 2.92–3.00) and 0174 = 2.97 (six stamps, 2.72/2.88/2.88/3.00/3.18/3.14 — the wider spread is pure quantisation on a ~23 px risk leg). Two further schematics: 0199 = 2.907 and 0202 = 2.909. EXCEPTIONS, all structurally explained: Range-STRATEGY cards S1/S2 (0179, 0182) = 2.72 and S3/S4 (0184, 0186) = 1.83 — brackets pinned to range geometry, with S3/S4 lower because both trade AFTER a deviation above the range so the stop must clear that excursion while the target stays the range low; the two SHORT entry-model cards 0197 = 1.37 and 0198 = 1.36 (a third cluster, 0.01 apart — a template, not coincidence); and 0183 realises 1.62R where its own schematic advertises 2.72R. LIVE EXECUTIONS RUN 1.4–1.7R. MEASUREMENT METHOD: quote R:R from stroke CENTRES, not outer edges — strokes are 4–5 px and risk legs are short, so the choice moves a ratio by ~6%; 0202 reads 2.75 edge-to-edge and 2.909 centre-to-centre, and the ratio and the method vouch for each other. Also check for an overdrawn border before quoting (one ratio was published as 3.48 and corrected to 4.13).
rules.inputs: Measured bracket pixel geometry (risk leg, reward leg) from stroke centres.
rules.output: measured_rr + card_family hint.
rules.citation: §8 measurement discipline; §9 IM30; §9.J IM102 (house-ratio note), IM106–IM109, IM114
rules.notes: Carry the doctrine-vs-practice gap into the learning loop: the ruled preference is ≈3R (GATE-025), the illustrations draw ≈2.9R, and the trader's own realised executions in the corpus run 1.4–1.7R — “the cards sell ~2.7–2.9R and the worked examples realise 1.4–1.7R”.

rules.name: CASE 001–010 stop-hunt setup-quality verdict (a third, unlinked risk overlay)
rules.statement: The course's own setup grader is BINARY with two options per grade, and it grades a setup ENTIRELY by stop-loss-hunt state. HIGH PROBABILITY → “Option 1 (Regular Risk 1% - 1R)” / “Option 2 (Increased Risk 1.5% - 1.5R)”, risk box labelled `1/1.5R` (cards 0209, 0211, 0213, 0215, 0217). LOW PROBABILITY → “Option 1 (Do Not Take The Trade)” / “Option 2 (Reduce The Risk 0.5% - 0.5R)”, risk box labelled `0.5R` (cards 0208, 0210, 0212, 0214, 0216). The split is exactly 5 LOW / 5 HIGH and the table is VERIFIED CORRECT exactly as printed. There are TWO verdict classes, not three — no card prints 1% alone, no card prints 1.5% alone; any reproduction treating “0.5% / 1% / 1.5%” as three setup-quality states misstates the source. Qualifying pattern for HIGH: a completed sweep BEHIND the entry, a break (MSB/BOS) in the trade direction after it, entry at the fresh IMB left by the breaking leg, and untaken liquidity AHEAD as fuel. LOW: untaken liquidity still behind/beneath the entry, or trading against a fresh sweep. The `0.5R`/`1R`/`1.5R` figures are POSITION-SIZING (stake) instructions, entirely independent of the constant ~2.9 drawn bracket geometry — reading “0.5R” as a 0.5 reward-to-risk trade misreads the table. Bracket SIZE does not encode the verdict either (risk legs 45–79.5 px with no verdict split; 0215 is a HIGH card on a smaller risk leg than three of the five LOW cards).
rules.inputs: Stop-hunt state around the entry (swept-behind vs untaken-behind), break direction after the sweep, freshness of the entry imbalance, untaken liquidity ahead.
rules.output: case_verdict ∈ {LOW, HIGH} + its two-option menu — TELEMETRY ONLY until reconciled with the box-grade × disturbance matrix.
rules.citation: §9 IM30 (fills the image-only gap at §2 E8); §7.1 item 9; §10.A.1 (“Also not linked to anything”); §10.F.2 item 14
rules.notes: This is a THIRD risk overlay in the corpus, using entirely different inputs from box-grade × disturbance, and the PDF does not mention it at all. Do not merge it with GATE-032 and do not silently discard it — log both and let the learning loop attribute outcomes. A worked LOW case with a measured gate: CASE 007's “Extremely Close Untaken LIQ” ray sits 7.5 px below the stop (31 px below the entry) — the stop-to-pool gap is 12% of the risk leg, so “extremely close” is literal and any hunt of the pool takes the trade out. The sibling rule is drawn on 0204 as “Extremely Close But Not Hunted LIQ” with the callout “Almost EQL HIGH — It is best to wait for LIQ HUNTED!” (§9.E IM29).

rules.name: Correlate agreement is sign-relative — never the raw directional sign
rules.statement: For every panel in the layout, the DISTURBED/ALIGNED verdict is an AGREEMENT value, not a direction. It MUST be derived as agreement = sign(observed_order_flow) x sign(expected_sign), where expected_sign comes from the asset's role in the fixed roster (GATE-008): for a BTC long, BTC/ETH/TOTAL expect BULLISH and USDT.D expects BEARISH; mirrored for a short. An engine that scores panels with a raw directional function (bullish +1 / neutral 0 / bearish -1) and then feeds that score to the disturbance count INVERTS the negative-correlated asset: a falling USDT.D — which is exactly what a BTC long requires — is scored -1 and counted as disturbed. In the four-panel BTC roster that single inversion moves the disturbance grade by one level on every setup, which moves the risk-matrix cell (GATE-032) and can turn a tradable LIGHT into a HEAVY hard skip (GATE-001) or the reverse. If both a directional score and an agreement score are implemented they MUST be named distinctly (directional_sign vs agreement_state) and MUST NOT be summed or share a function.
rules.inputs: Per-panel observed_order_flow; the panel's role (MAIN/POSITIVE/NEGATIVE) and expected_sign from GATE-008; the intended side of the trade.
rules.output: agreement_state in {ALIGNED, NEUTRAL, DISTURBED} per panel, recorded alongside observed_order_flow and expected_sign so the derivation is re-checkable from the record alone; feeds the count in GATE-002.
rules.citation: §10.D D-6 and D-7 with the ⚠ collision note (“For a BTC long, a falling USDT.D is −1 under D-6 and +1 under D-7… Any engine that sums the two, or reuses one function for both, inverts the negative-correlated asset”); §2 F1 [R] and §2 F2 [R] (PDF Q7, pp.16–18); §10.A.2 row 1; §9.F IM31/IM33
rules.notes: D-6 and D-7 are themselves class [D] engine machinery and must never be quoted as strategy. What IS doctrine, and what this rule enforces, is the roster with signs (§2 F1/F2, ruled at Q7 p.16) and the resulting requirement that USDT.D moving OPPOSITE to BTC is agreement, not disagreement. The rule was absent from v1.0.0 entirely even though the codex flags the failure mode explicitly.

rules.name: Structure Box construction (precondition for any box grade)
rules.statement: A structure box exists only once a break event (MSB or BOS) has printed. Construct it from the price of the swing that was broken back to that swing, ending at the breaking candle: box time-span = swing_bar → break_bar; box price-span = swing_extreme → break price. The box's extreme (low for an up-leg, high for a down-leg) IS the Strong Low / Strong High. Either break type may create a box (the slide labels the box-birth break 'MSB / BoS'). No box ⇒ no box grade ⇒ the risk matrix cannot be looked up and no trade may be sized.
rules.inputs: Execution-timeframe (30M/15M/5M) candle series for the traded asset; the confirmed swing-point series on that TF; the break-event stream (MSB/BOS) with the identity of the swing each break consumed; leg direction.
rules.output: StructureBox{id, direction, swing_bar, break_bar, box_high, box_low, strong_swing_price, birth_break_type ∈ {MSB,BOS}} or null
rules.citation: §2 A8 (056_Structure_Boxes.md: 'When there is a new BOS or MSB that happens then a structure box comes to life. You can draw this box from the swing low/high that is broken until the moment of break'); §9.A IM1 (Structure_Writing_And_Car_Analogy/0311 — every drawn box tagged '(SB)'); §9.A IM3 (0321 labels the box-birth break 'MSB / BoS')
rules.notes: §9 IM1 is what resolves the journal's 'SB' token as Structure Box; it is a drawn tag, not a spelled-out expansion.

rules.name: STANDARD Structure Box
rules.statement: Grade the box STANDARD when the pullback inside it taps an imbalance/gap zone ONLY: no wick trades beyond any prior internal swing inside the box (below for a long setup, above for a short), and no fake MSB prints. Fuel = imbalance alone (1 component). Recorded consequence: the strong low/high CAN be tested. Risk key = 1.00% at no disturbance.
rules.inputs: StructureBox from GRADE-001; the imbalance/gap inventory on the same TF with fill state; the internal swing series inside the box's time span; the extremes of the pullback excursion.
rules.output: box_grade = STANDARD, plus evidence tuple {imbalance_tap: true, inner_sweep: false, fake_msb: false}
rules.citation: §2 A8 (057_Structure_Super_Box_Intro.md, 025, 063_Super_Box.md, 023_Questionnaire.md — 'a standard structure box which is only fueled by an imbalance no inner liquidity… so i'm taking a low risk trade or no trade at all'); §8 'Box grading (drives risk %)'; §9.A IM5 card STANDARD STRUCTURE BOX (Questionnaire/0262 — 'Smart Money only uses imbalances! Not tested SHORT or LONG traders yet! STRONG LOW can be tested!'); §9.A IM4 left panel 'Normal Structure BOX / Normal INNER POI'

rules.name: SUPER Structure Box
rules.statement: Grade SUPER when the pullback does BOTH: (a) fills/taps the imbalance zone, AND (b) sweeps inner liquidity — a wick beyond a prior internal swing on ONE side only (the i-LIQ sweep that traps the early traders positioned in the trade's own direction). Fuel = IMB + LIQ (2 components). Recorded consequence: the strong low/high has LESS CHANCE of being tested. POI grade = 'BETTER POI IMB'. Risk key = 1.25% at no disturbance.
rules.inputs: StructureBox from GRADE-001; imbalance inventory + fill state; internal swing series and the pullback's wick extremes on each side; the identity of the swept internal swing.
rules.output: box_grade = SUPER, plus evidence tuple {imbalance_tap: true, inner_sweep: true (with swept swing id + wick price), fake_msb: false}
rules.citation: §2 A9 (025, 057, 063_Super_Box.md, 023, 105_Putting_all_together.md — 'we do not only use imbalance, we also sweep inner liquidity before moving, strong low has much less chance of being tested… so i'm taking a moderated risk trade'); §8; §9.A IM5 middle card 'SUPER BOX (The INDUCEMENT)' (untitled/0541, recovered via §9.K IM119 — ONE dashed i-LIQ Sweep, one full can 'IMB + LIQ'); §9.A IM4 right panel
rules.notes: The middle THEORY card was missing from the original IM5 and was added on audit from the 053 DB attachments (§9.K IM119); it is the only source that states the SUPER tier's 'less chance of being tested' wording.

rules.name: MANIPULATED Structure Box
rules.statement: Grade MANIPULATED only when ALL THREE are present around one structure: (1) an imbalance/gap tap; (2) an inner liquidity sweep trapping one side; (3) a fake MSB trapping the other side — i.e. wicks beyond BOTH a prior high AND a prior low around the same box, so long and short traders are trapped in the same structure. Fuel = IMB + LIQ + LIQ (3 components, two full cans). Recorded consequence: the strong low/high SHALL NOT be tested. POI grade = 'PERFECT POI IMB'. Risk key = 1.50% at no disturbance.
rules.inputs: StructureBox from GRADE-001; imbalance inventory; internal swing series with wick excursions on BOTH sides; the fake-MSB classification from GRADE-008.
rules.output: box_grade = MANIPULATED, plus evidence tuple {imbalance_tap, inner_sweep (side + swing id), fake_msb (side + break bar)}
rules.citation: §2 A10 (023_Questionnaire.md: 'I have a manipulated structure box where both long and short traders trapped at the same structure, now the strong low shall not be tested at all… so i'm taking a high risk trade'; 063_Super_Box.md; 105); §8; §9.A IM5 card MANIPULATED SUPER BOX (Super_Box/0726 — upper dashed 'i-LIQ Sweep' + lower 'i-LIQ Sweep / Fake MSB', 'STRONG LOW shall not be tested!')

rules.name: Box-grade ordinal invariant (fuel count, not shape)
rules.statement: The three grades form ONE ordinal ladder keyed to the count of fuel components detected, not three unrelated shapes: Standard = 1 (IMB) → 'can be tested'; Super = 2 (IMB+LIQ) → 'less chance of being tested'; Manipulated = 3 (IMB+LIQ+LIQ) → 'shall not be tested'. A grader whose output is not monotonic in the detected fuel-component count is non-conforming. Record the count alongside the grade so conformance can be tested without re-deriving the geometry.
rules.inputs: The evidence tuples emitted by GRADE-002/003/004.
rules.output: fuel_component_count ∈ {1,2,3} and the strong-swing retest expectation label
rules.citation: §9.A IM5 (the three THEORY cards: jerrycan count part-filled/1 full/2 full and the NORMAL → BETTER → PERFECT POI IMB ladder); §9.A IM2 (the printed equation 'OUR CAR FUEL = LIQ + IMB')

rules.name: DEFECT — two incompatible definitions of the Manipulated box
rules.statement: The source carries two incompatible definitions. §8 / §2 A10 / §9.A IM5 require an imbalance-or-gap tap in EVERY box grade. PDF Q10 (pp.22–24) defines the Manipulated Structure Box as sweep + counter-trend MSB + both sides trapped + continuation, with NO imbalance tap — and never defines Standard or Super at all, despite making all three the key of the risk table. The engine MUST implement the §8 key (imbalance tap mandatory in all three grades) and MUST NOT build the grader from Q10 alone: because the box grade sets the risk %, an engine built from Q10 will mis-grade boxes and therefore mis-size every trade.
rules.inputs: n/a — specification-level blocker.
rules.output: A declared, versioned choice of definition recorded in telemetry, flagged as unratified.
rules.citation: §8 'Box grading (drives risk %)' — 'Keep this key — the PDF does not replace it'; §10.F.2 item 15; §2 A3 [R] (PDF Q10, pp.22–24)
rules.triage_note: MANIPULATED = imbalance tap AND inner-liquidity sweep AND fake MSB. Build from the workspace key, not from the PDF Q10 definition.

rules.name: POI-timing gate — grade only after all manipulation has printed
rules.statement: A box may be graded, and its POI qualified, only after ALL manipulation belonging to that box has already printed. Grading a partially formed box — e.g. emitting MANIPULATED before the second-side trap has printed — is an early entry and a conformance failure. Evaluate on completed price action strictly to the left of the decision bar, never on an in-progress pullback.
rules.inputs: Decision bar index; the box's completed evidence tuple; a look-ahead guard proving no evidence bar postdates the decision bar.
rules.output: poi_qualified boolean + the bar index at which the last manipulation component completed
rules.citation: §9.A IM6 (RR_Ratio_and_Setup_Risk/0884 — 'Preventing early entry! You find your POI after all MANIPULATION DONE!', with the dotted 'now' divider and the backward-pointing 'You observe past actions' arrow)

rules.name: Fake-MSB classification (component 3 of the Manipulated grade)
rules.statement: Classify a break as a POTENTIAL FAKE MSB when this sequence is observed: (1) the HTF target is still valid; (2) a liquidity sweep occurs; (3) a temporary structural break prints against the main direction; (4) genuine reversal confirmation is absent; (5) price continues toward the HTF target. Both long and short traders must end up trapped inside the same structure. The engine is FORBIDDEN to define a fake MSB using fixed rules such as 'reversal within N candles', a maximum candle count, or a fixed time delay — 'those are implementation shortcuts rather than trading concepts'. The MSB is never the objective; it is one component of a larger liquidity manipulation.
rules.inputs: The active HTF target and its cleared/uncleared state; the sweep event stream; the counter-direction break event; the post-break continuation evidence; the trapped-side inventory (stops on both sides of the box).
rules.output: fake_msb {true/false, break_bar, swept_side, trapped_sides[], htf_target_id}
rules.citation: §2 A3 [R] (PDF Q10, pp.22–24: 'the MSB is never the objective'; the five-step engine sequence; 'Both long and short traders become trapped inside the same structure'; the no-candle-count prohibition); §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER
rules.notes: Step (4) — 'lack of genuine reversal confirmation' — has no operational test anywhere, and the trader explicitly declined to supply candle-count or time-delay proxies. The positive detector cannot be fully specified from the source.

rules.name: WHICH box does the grade refer to?
rules.statement: The grade that keys the risk table is not bound to a specific box anywhere in the source. It is left open in three separate places (strategic target selection Step 1, context validation Step 3, and the invented momentum score's component 6), and the source never says whether it means the ENTRY box on the execution timeframe or the box at the destination. The engine must pick one — the entry box on the execution TF is the reading most consistent with 023 Step 6, which grades the box the entry sits in — declare the choice in telemetry, and flag it as unratified rather than silently assuming it.
rules.inputs: n/a — specification-level decision.
rules.output: box_scope ∈ {ENTRY_BOX_EXEC_TF, DESTINATION_BOX} recorded per decision
rules.citation: §10.D D-1 component-6 note ('the PDF never says which box is meant… a question it leaves open in three separate places'); §10.F; §3.2 Part 1 step 6 (023_Questionnaire.md — the fuel check that classifies standard/super/manipulated is applied to the entry box)

rules.name: Disturbance grade — absolute count of disturbed correlated assets
rules.statement: disturbance_grade is a function of the COUNT of correlated assets flagged disturbed: 0 → NO_DISTURBANCE; exactly 1 → LIGHT; 2 or more → HEAVY. This is an absolute count of assets — not a ratio, not a percentage of the layout, not a score. Evaluate at the entry decision bar, on the alignment timeframe, which equals the execution timeframe.
rules.inputs: The correlated-asset roster from GRADE-012; per-asset disturbance verdicts from GRADE-013; the alignment timeframe; the intended trade direction; the entry decision bar.
rules.output: disturbance_grade ∈ {NO, LIGHT, HEAVY} + disturbed_asset_ids[] + the off-condition id that fired for each
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q9, pp.20–21: 'Light Disturbance: Exactly one correlated asset is disturbed'; 'Heavy Disturbance: Two or more correlated assets are disturbed'); §3.7 step 2; §9.F IM36 (Questionnaire/0281 shows ONE offending pane = Light; 0287 shows TWO = Heavy)

rules.name: HEAVY disturbance is a hard filter
rules.statement: HEAVY disturbance ⇒ risk = 0% ⇒ NO TRADE, regardless of the structure-box grade. This is a gate, not a size reduction. Implement the 'hard filter' formulation; do NOT implement the softer 'the trade should usually be skipped' or the workspace's 'i will 90% skip the trade' — an engine cannot implement 'usually' or '90%'. The three statements exist in the source at different strictnesses and must never be quoted interchangeably; the latest and most explicit one wins.
rules.inputs: disturbance_grade from GRADE-010.
rules.output: trade_permitted = false and risk_pct = 0 when HEAVY
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q14, p.29: 'Heavy Disturbance is a hard filter: no trade regardless of the Structure Box'); §10.A.1; §10.F.1 defect D6b; dead prose at §2 F5 / 027_RR_Ratio_and_Setup_Risk.md

rules.name: Correlated-asset roster and alignment timeframe (the denominator)
rules.statement: For BTC the layout is fixed by name: main = BTC; positive correlation = ETH and TOTAL; negative correlation = USDT.D — exactly four panels; there is no panel called 'total dominance'. All assets must be checked on the SAME timeframe when confirming the entry, and that timeframe is the execution timeframe. Expected order-flow vector for a BTC long: BTC bullish, ETH bullish, TOTAL bullish, USDT.D bearish; mirrored for a short.
rules.inputs: Instrument being traded; the layout roster; the chosen execution timeframe; candle series for all four symbols on that TF, time-aligned.
rules.output: roster[] with per-asset expected_sign, and alignment_timeframe (must equal execution_timeframe)
rules.citation: §2 F1 [R] and §2 I2 [R] (PDF Q7, p.16); §9.F IM33 (live layout 'PA Crypto' = BTCUSDT.P / USDT.D / TOTAL / ETHUSDT.P, all 15m, symbol-sync OFF); §7.1.7 (resolved)
rules.notes: Only the same-timeframe requirement is stated firmly. The specific set {5M, 15M, 30M} is hedged three times in the source ('usually', 'such as', 'sometimes') — do not quote it as a fixed roster.

rules.name: Per-asset 'off' condition detector
rules.statement: An asset is DISTURBED when it no longer supports the expected trade direction while the majority of correlated assets still do. Evaluate at least the trader's six: (1) order flow opposite to what the correlation implies; (2) fails the expected MSB/BOS while others confirmed; (3) moving toward a completely different liquidity objective; (4) reacts significantly before or after the others; (5) different momentum profile; (6) creates a structural reversal while others trend. Also evaluate the drawn six, which must be kept because neither list is declared exhaustive: ENTRY-side — no MSB, no BOS, never swept LIQ before MSB; TARGET-side — no clear target, target already cleared, stuck between LIQ points.
rules.inputs: Per-asset candle series on the alignment TF; per-asset break-event stream (i-MSB / i-BoS); per-asset sweep state before each break; per-asset target inventory and cleared state; per-asset momentum regime (GRADE-039); the expected sign from GRADE-012.
rules.output: per-asset {disturbed: bool, off_condition_id, evidence_bar}
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q9, p.20 — the six named 'off' conditions); §9.F IM36 (the drawn taxonomy: ENTRY ALIGNMENT DISTURBANCE 0281/0282/0283 vs TARGET ALIGNMENT DISTURBANCE 0284/0285/0286); §9.F IM37 (glyph/colour grammar: red 'LIQ OPEN' = liquidity un-swept before an MSB ⇒ invalid break precondition)
rules.notes: The two lists are compatible but not identical — the PDF adds 'different momentum profile' and 'structural reversal' and DROPS the drawn 'never swept LIQ before MSB'. Neither list is declared exhaustive. The two lists are ONE PREDICATE WITH TWO ENUMERATIONS: every drawn slide in both families closes “It causes DISTURBANCE (Reduce the RISK)”. Keep both. The CAUSES axis is OPEN — his framing is a sampler (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:79 “all kinds of possible examples”, :85 “what else can we talk about”, :91 “here's another idea”) and the governing rule is a DEFINITION at 065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:83 — “if the correlated asset do not act the way they are supposed to act i call it magic disturbance”. The SEVERITY axis IS CLOSED and stated: none / light / heavy. OFF_4 IS NOW IMPLEMENTABLE and comes off NOT_EVALUATED: lead/lag is a LEVEL STATE to him, never a clock — “having reaction before sweeping the close liquidity” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:85), “already swept the liquidity but other assets are still trying to reach the liquidity” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:89), “most Altcoins lag, they will have open targets to clear” (066_Magic_Quadrant_For_Altcoins.md:9). NEGATIVE CASE, to prevent false positives: being further along the MSB->BOS sequence is explicitly NOT a disturbance — “it is fine it makes no difference for me” (065_Magic_Alignment_Entry.md:19). Uses no correlation coefficient, no candle count and no clock, so it complies with his own bans. OFF_5 (different momentum profile) STAYS NOT_EVALUATED — it depends on the un-fittable momentum-regime boundary. [ENGINEERING] to pin: the shared evaluation instant, and what counts as swept/cleared (wick touch vs close-through) applied identically to every asset. DO NOT gate detectors behind a “majority of other panels aligned” precondition: on a 3-correlate roster with 2 disturbed it suppresses both detections, drops the grade from HEAVY to NONE, and sizes a full-risk trade in a market the trader would skip.
rules.open_half_note: Ships 4 of 6 conditions today. Round 2 unblocked OFF_4 (condition 4) — it is now implementable as a level-state comparison and must come off NOT_EVALUATED; that is its own task. Only OFF_5 (condition 5, different momentum profile) remains genuinely unevaluable.

rules.name: Disturbance is structural, never statistical
rules.statement: Disturbance must be determined from structural agreement only. The engine is FORBIDDEN to determine it from a correlation coefficient (e.g. 'the correlation dropped below 0.75'), a fixed number of candles ('the asset must confirm within two candles'), or a fixed time delay ('the MSB must occur within five minutes'). Separately, the ±80% correlation figure is an asset-SELECTION rule used only to decide which assets belong in the layout — it is NOT the trade-confirmation metric, and the engine must not compute a rolling correlation coefficient as a live trade filter.
rules.inputs: n/a — an input prohibition applied to GRADE-010 and GRADE-013.
rules.output: A conformance assertion: no correlation-coefficient, candle-count or time-delay term appears in the disturbance computation.
rules.citation: §2 F5 [R] (PDF Q9, pp.20–21: 'The strategy evaluates structural agreement, not statistical correlation'); §2 F2 [R] and §9.F IM31 [R] (PDF Q7, p.18); §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER

rules.name: Six admissible agreement forms — simultaneity is not required
rules.statement: Alignment must NOT require all assets to print the same structure on the same candle ('that would be too rigid'). Six forms of agreement are admissible: all assets MSB in the same entry window; some already MSB'd and now continuing with BOS; one leading / one lagging but still moving toward the same idea; positives not fighting the main asset; the negative moving opposite as expected; similar target logic (liquidity, imbalance, key levels, institutional levels). Governing maxim, printed on the slides: 'MSB or BoS is NOT the KEY! TREND is the KEY! Trending in the same direction!' The engine must not confirm alignment by a fixed cross-asset metric such as 'the last BOS on the 15-minute chart matches on all assets'.
rules.inputs: Per-asset break-event stream and order-flow direction on the alignment TF; per-asset target inventory; the entry window definition.
rules.output: per-asset agreement_form_id (one of six) or null, feeding GRADE-013
rules.citation: §2 F1 [R] (PDF Q7, pp.15–17); §9.F IM34 (Magic_Alignment_Entry/0763, 0765, 0767 — the ENTRY ALIGNMENT slides, including the mixed 'some assets could have done MSB already' state)

rules.name: Disturbance count does not normalise to layout size
rules.statement: The count is absolute and does not scale with the number of correlates. RULED round 2: the MAIN asset does NOT count toward it (see GATE-004). 2-of-2 (the Essential layout) is 100% disagreement and sensible; 2-of-3 (the BTC layout) is Heavy; but the workspace explicitly permits five positive and five negative correlates and calls that layout STRONGER — under the absolute count, 2-of-10 would still grade Heavy and skip the trade, penalising exactly the layout the trader prefers. The roster is therefore FROZEN to the four-panel layout (GATE-003) rather than converted to a ratio, and the engine must not silently invent either.
rules.inputs: n/a — specification-level blocker on GRADE-010.
rules.output: A declared, versioned policy: layout_size_frozen (bool) and main_asset_counts (bool), recorded in telemetry.
rules.citation: §10.F.1 defect D5b; §10.F.2 item 11; §2 F5 [R] caveat; §2 F1 (106_Examples.md — 'you can find five positive and five negative correlated assets which will make your entry even stronger')
rules.notes: TWO COUNTS OVER TWO DIFFERENT SETS. ALIGNMENT includes the main panel — his own handwritten note card “PERFECT MAGIC ALIGNMENT! / 4 MSB + 4 BPR = 4 Assets ALIGNED! / ZERO DISTURBANCE!” on a 4-panel BTCUSDT.P + USDT.D/TOTAL/ETHUSDT.P screenshot (images/Putting_All_Together/0443_05509bb4.png). DISTURBANCE is tagged on correlates only: the main pane is never tagged across the drawn slides (images/Questionnaire/0280-0287, images/Magic_Alignment_Setup/). SHIPS AS INFERENCE, NOT AS HIS RULE — the corpus prints no explicit exemption sentence, so main_asset_counted is a DECLARED PARAMETER carrying authority=ENGINEERING and ratified=false in `values`, never a bare doctrine value. THE COMPENSATING GATE IS REQUIRED AND DOES NOT YET EXIST: emit main_asset_state = SETUP_INVALID as a hard upstream skip that never reaches grading. NOT OPTIONAL — exclusion alone lowers disturbed_count, lightens the grade and RAISES the risk cell, so it is a systematic tilt toward LARGER positions rather than a neutral gap. STATE OF PLAY, recorded rather than smoothed over: MAIN_ASSET_COUNTS=False has been live in shadow since commit fd52295 on 2026-08-08 (gate_002_disturbance.py:356, wired at evaluator.py:351), so the exclusion has run WITHOUT its gate. main_asset_state was added to TELEMETRY_SCHEMA.json by T-0027 but is NOT yet in setup_evaluation.required, because no producer computes the verdict; SETUP_INVALID is emitted by nothing. THIS ROW IS NOT SETTLED until the gate exists — tracked in KNOWN_ISSUES.md. Layout authority: 064_Magic_Alignment_Setup.md:19 “there's no trading without the setup, i cannot take a single trade without the setup”; 064_Magic_Alignment_Setup.md:23 the +/-80% correlate rule; images/Magic_Alignment_Setup/0738_5da5632d.png “3+ Layout System”.

values.main_asset_counted_basis: INFERENCE from two counts over two different sets — the corpus prints no explicit exemption sentence. Confidence: medium-high.

rules.name: The 9-cell risk matrix (box grade × disturbance → risk %)
rules.statement: risk_pct = LOOKUP(box_grade, disturbance_grade), implemented as a literal lookup table with exactly these values: Manipulated/No = 1.50% (0.015); Super/No = 1.25% (0.0125); Standard/No = 1.00% (0.01); Manipulated/Light = 0.75% (0.0075); Super/Light = 0.50% (0.005); Standard/Light = 0.25% (0.0025); ANY box / Heavy = 0% (skip). Source of truth is the 'Risk % Setups' database's Risk Alignment column, which the nine cells reproduce exactly. The 076 prose tier (2% / 1.5% / 1%) is DEAD for the engine, and with it the 2% ceiling and the drawn pairing '2% = 2R reserved for a 4R Perfect setup' — both become unreachable cells, retired by omission rather than by argument.
rules.inputs: box_grade from GRADE-002/003/004; disturbance_grade from GRADE-010.
rules.output: risk_pct (decimal) + the matrix cell id that produced it
rules.citation: §2 H3 [O]; §10.A.1 (PDF Q9, p.21; Q14, p.29 — 'let's use the latest Risk % Setups database as the source of truth'); §3.7 step 3; 053_untitled.md; §10.B O3; §9.G IM40 (the retired pairing)

rules.name: DEFECT — the 'base risk × 0.5' modifier double-sizes the most common grade
rules.statement: DO NOT implement the proposed 'base risk + disturbance modifier' refactor (No = ×1, Light = ×0.5, Heavy = ×0). It claims to produce 'exactly the same results as the table' and does not. Manipulated 1.50 × 0.5 = 0.75% matches; but Super 1.25 × 0.5 = 0.625% against the table's 0.50% (+0.125 pp, 25% more risk), and Standard 1.00 × 0.5 = 0.50% against the table's 0.25% — EXACTLY DOUBLE, on the most common grade. On a $100,000 account a Standard box with light disturbance would be sized at $500 instead of $250. The true relation is SUBTRACTIVE and exact for all three grades: Light = No − 0.75 percentage points. Equivalent per-box multipliers are ×0.50 / ×0.40 / ×0.25 — not a single ×0.5. Keep the lookup table. The defect is downstream-only: both printed source tables are verified clean, so an engine that reads them verbatim is safe and only the 'cleaner' restatement is not.
rules.inputs: n/a — a prohibition on the implementation of GRADE-017.
rules.output: A conformance assertion: no multiplicative disturbance modifier appears in the sizing path.
rules.citation: §10.A.1 DEFECT block (PDF Q14, p.29); §10.D D-10; §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER; §2 H3 warning line
rules.triage_note: Same defect as GATE-033, second id.

rules.name: The Risk Altcoin column — half the matrix is unruled
rules.statement: The source database has TWO risk outputs per row: Risk Alignment (ruled on, GRADE-017) and Risk Altcoin (0.0075 / 0.005 / 0.0025), which is disturbance-INVARIANT — identical at No and at Light — a structure no base-×-modifier scheme can express at all. The ruling declares the whole database authoritative and then every supplied number covers only Risk Alignment: 9 of the 18 cells are unanswered, whether the engine trades altcoins at all is unstated, and 'Heavy = hard filter' is only ASSUMED to override the database's non-zero altcoin Heavy cells (0.0075 / 0.05 / 0.0025). The 0.05 outlier is thereby made moot without ever being reconciled. The engine must refuse to size an altcoin trade rather than interpolate.
rules.inputs: instrument_class ∈ {aligned_major, altcoin}; box_grade; disturbance_grade.
rules.output: risk_pct for altcoins = UNDEFINED (refuse) until ruled.
rules.citation: §10.A.1 'The second column nobody addressed'; §10.F.2 item 13; §7.1.3; 053_untitled.md; §2 F6 (066_Magic_Quadrant_For_Altcoins.md — 'we can not rely on any kind of magic alignments when we trade Altcoins')
rules.triage_note: PARTIAL: ship risk_pct(altcoin) = f(box_grade) = {0.0075, 0.005, 0.0025}, disturbance-invariant. The Heavy-override half stays open (trader Q).
rules.open_half_note: Ships the altcoin box-grade scale; the Heavy-override half is unresolved (trader Q).
rules.notes: ROUND 2 — THE CONSTANT IS FLAT, NON-GATING, AND CARRIES THE TRADER'S OWN HEDGE. No scaling rule exists in either source, IN EITHER DIRECTION — flatness is an INFERENCE from the numbers being stated unqualified, not a ruling. His hedges, in his own words: 0.30% is “an initial calibration value and may be refined during validation” (answers Q4); ~1% are “approximate calibration values and should only be used as supporting information” (answers Q6); ~0.2% is “an engineering guideline, not a strict market rule” (answers Q8); the news rule “does not use a fixed number of minutes”. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS NOT HIS: the “BTC on the 1H chart and BTC on the Weekly chart have completely different imbalance sizes” sentence is PRIOR-AI-ASSISTANT REGISTER (bracketed by “Option 2 (What I recommend)”, “For example, tell him:”, “I would tell your developer this:”, “My suggestion”) and is scoped to momentum-imbalance SIZE classification, where no fixed percentage was ever adopted. It does not bear on these constants. His actual bans and their scope: momentum is “not defined by candle body size, ATR ratios, or a fixed number” (answers Q5); a disturbance is “not determined by correlation coefficients, a fixed number of candles, or a time delay” (answers Q9). EACH PERCENTAGE'S DENOMINATOR IS UNSTATED and must be declared by the implementer and stamped on every record. [ENGINEERING] GRADE-019 SPECIFICALLY: this row's own gap is the Risk Altcoin column, not a percentage constant. The altcoin box-grade scale ships disturbance-invariant {0.0075, 0.005, 0.0025}; the Heavy-override half stays open and needs the trader. The engine must REFUSE to size an altcoin trade rather than interpolate.

rules.name: E8 / CASE setup quality is BINARY — two verdict classes, not three
rules.statement: The stop-loss-hunt setup-quality grader emits exactly TWO verdict classes, each carrying two options — never three. LOW PROBABILITY → Option 1 'Do Not Take The Trade' | Option 2 'Reduce The Risk 0.5% - 0.5R', in-chart risk box labelled '0.5R'. HIGH PROBABILITY → Option 1 'Regular Risk 1% - 1R' | Option 2 'Increased Risk 1.5% - 1.5R', in-chart risk box labelled '1/1.5R'. Verified across all ten cards: no card prints 1% alone, no card prints 1.5% alone, no card offers a third grade. The split is exactly 5 LOW (0208, 0210, 0212, 0214, 0216) / 5 HIGH (0209, 0211, 0213, 0215, 0217). Any implementation that emits '0.5% / 1% / 1.5%' as three setup-quality states misstates the source — that exact error already existed downstream in the corpus and was corrected on audit.
rules.inputs: The setup's sweep/break/imbalance/liquidity evidence from GRADE-021.
rules.output: case_verdict ∈ {LOW, HIGH} + case_option ∈ {1,2} + the risk figure that option implies
rules.citation: §9.E IM30 (Technical_Concepts/0208–0217, all ten cards re-read by calibrated measurement); §7.3(b) item 9; §10.A.1 correction note; §10.F.2 item 14; CODEX_FOLLOWUPS.md 'Batch J'

rules.name: CASE qualifying pattern (the HIGH/LOW test)
rules.statement: HIGH requires ALL of: (a) a COMPLETED liquidity sweep BEHIND the entry; (b) a break (MSB or BOS) in the trade direction AFTER that sweep; (c) the entry sits at the FRESH imbalance left by the breaking leg; (d) untaken liquidity AHEAD of the trade as fuel. LOW is either of: untaken liquidity still resting behind/beneath the entry (it will be hunted through the stop), or trading against a fresh sweep. Emit which of (a)–(d) held, and the price/id of any untaken pool behind the entry.
rules.inputs: Entry price and stop price; the liquidity inventory on the setup TF with taken/untaken state (including diagonal LIQ POOL objects along staircases); the break-event stream after the sweep; the fresh imbalance left by the breaking leg; the intended trade direction; any standing HTF demand/supply zone the target would land inside.
rules.output: case_verdict + the four booleans + untaken_pool_behind{price, distance_as_pct_of_risk_leg}
rules.citation: §9.E IM30 ('The qualifying pattern for HIGH is: a completed sweep BEHIND the entry, a break (MSB/BOS) in the trade direction after it, entry at the fresh IMB left by the breaking leg, and untaken liquidity AHEAD as fuel. LOW is: untaken liquidity still behind/beneath the entry, or trading against a fresh sweep.')

rules.name: The ten CASE cards as the labelled conformance corpus
rules.statement: Ten hand-labelled reference setups exist and are verified correct exactly as printed; use them as the regression fixture for the E8 grader. 001 LOW — range with un-hunted LIQ rays BOTH above and below; long off a minor BREAK + small IMB. 002 HIGH — HTF DEMAND box + 'HTF LIQ SWEEP or DEMAND' at the low → MSB → entry at the first fresh IMB; large unfilled IMB overhead + LIQ as target. 003 LOW — after HTF LIQ SWEEP + MSB + BOS, a late long at a second shallower IMB while a deeper unfilled IMB with resting LIQ remains BELOW. 004 HIGH — downtrend with a dashed diagonal LIQ POOL along the lower highs; sweep into HTF DEMAND → bullish MSB → pullback into the fresh IMB. 005 LOW — up-staircase whose ascending LIQ POOL under the higher lows is still UNTAKEN; the pool arrow ends exactly at the stop box. 006 HIGH — post-MSB uptrend whose overhead pool has been taken (LIQ POOL SWEEP); deep retrace back into the origin IMB. 007 LOW — long from an IMB with 'Extremely Close Untaken LIQ' resting directly beneath it: measured 7.5 px below the stop, i.e. the stop-to-pool gap is 12% of the risk leg. 008 HIGH — old range highs broken into an S/R-flip level; on the retest a small LIQ SWEEP below the level, then MSB and a fresh IMB. 009 LOW — a SHORT on a bearish inner MSB against a fresh HTF-demand reaction, whose reward box base (347) sits 18 px INSIDE the standing demand zone (top 329); the series' only short. 010 HIGH — post-MSB consolidation with LIQ WAITING above; the long is taken only AFTER the LIQ SWEEP of the range lows into the POI box beneath.
rules.inputs: Chart images at images/Technical_Concepts/0208_2e84a5aa.png through 0217_16aad032.png.
rules.output: A pass/fail regression report: grader verdict vs printed verdict, per card.
rules.citation: §9.E IM30 table and Sources list; CODEX_FOLLOWUPS.md 'Batch J'
rules.notes: CASE 005's BOS count is flagged UNVERIFIED in the source ('five/six'); do not assert a count. CASE 009's flaw is geometric as well as narrative and is the strongest single test of a target-placement check.

rules.name: The ~2.9 house reward-to-risk ratio and its exceptions
rules.statement: The drawn reward-to-risk in the CASE series is CONSTANT and independent of verdict, stake, position size and direction: 0208 2.85 | 0209 2.89 | 0210 2.90 | 0211 2.87 | 0212 2.89 | 0213 2.87 | 0214 2.88 | 0215 2.93 | 0216 2.92 | 0217 2.87 — range 2.85–2.93, and 0216 (the series' only short, red risk box ABOVE green reward) still measures 2.92. This ~2.9 is the deck's HOUSE ratio wherever a bracket is illustrative: it also holds on the Range-Bias cards (0173 = 2.93, 0174 = 2.97). It has two structurally explained exceptions on the Range-STRATEGY cards, whose brackets are pinned to specific range geometry (S1/S2 = 2.72, S3/S4 = 1.83), while live executions run 1.4–1.7R. Use the measured ratio to identify which card family a frame belongs to; do NOT use it as a target rule and do NOT let it override the 2R floor / ~3R preference of the stop-selection layer.
rules.inputs: Measured bracket geometry, centre-to-centre (stroke centres, not outer edges: the choice moves a ratio by ~6%).
rules.output: measured_rr + inferred card family
rules.citation: §9.E IM30 CORRECTED block; §8 'Measurement discipline' and '~2.9:1 is the deck's house R:R'; §9.J IM102 rule 5; CODEX_FOLLOWUPS.md 'Batch J'

rules.name: E8 varies STAKE, never target geometry
rules.statement: '0.5R' / '1R' / '1.5R' on the CASE cards are POSITION-SIZE (stake) instructions and are entirely independent of the drawn ~2.9 reward-to-risk. Reading '0.5R' as a 0.5 reward-to-risk trade misreads the table. Bracket SIZE does not encode the verdict either: risk legs run 45–79.5 px with no verdict split — LOW cards measure 46, 59.5, 45, 60, 59.5 and HIGH cards 76, 79.5, 79.5, 56.5, 79.5, so 0215 is a HIGH card on a smaller risk leg than three of the five LOW cards. Only the RATIO is invariant. The previously recorded claim that 'risk % and bracket size always move together' is FALSE and withdrawn; so is 'the CASE series uses exactly two bracket stamps keyed to verdict', disproved by 0215.
rules.inputs: n/a — a reading rule applied to GRADE-020 and GRADE-023.
rules.output: A conformance assertion: the stake field and the reward-to-risk field are computed independently and never derived from one another.
rules.citation: §9.E IM30 CORRECTED block (verified by calibrated measurement of all ten cards); CODEX_FOLLOWUPS.md 'Batch J → CRITICAL READING RULE'
rules.runtime_assertion: PER RECORD: the reward-to-risk computation MUST NOT list stake/risk_pct among its inputs (data-lineage assertion over the telemetry's recorded inputs). CORPUS: across records, stake and reward-to-risk must show no dependence — stake varies across the 9-cell matrix while R:R holds the documented ~2.9 house ratio and its listed exceptions.
rules.team_lead_note: Adjudicated: kept HARD_GATE. The critic was right that independence cannot be proven from one record, but a lineage check can be — if R:R is computed FROM stake, the telemetry shows it. Per-record catches the mechanism; corpus-level catches the symptom.

rules.name: The CASE scale is a THIRD, unlinked risk overlay
rules.statement: The corpus contains three risk overlays with different inputs and nothing linking them: (1) box grade × disturbance → 1.50/1.25/1.00 → 0.75/0.50/0.25 → 0 (operative, GRADE-017); (2) the CASE stop-hunt verdict → skip or 0.5% (LOW), 1% or 1.5% (HIGH), keyed to stop-hunt state, which is the course's OWN sizing rule and is never mentioned in the rulings; (3) the retired 076 prose tier plus the drawn pairing '1% = 1R with a 2R Great setup / 2% = 2R reserved for a 4R Perfect setup'. It is undecided whether the CASE verdict gates, caps, replaces or merely annotates the matrix output. The engine must not invent a combination; it must compute both (1) and (2), record both, and apply only (1) until ruled.
rules.inputs: risk_pct from GRADE-017; case_verdict from GRADE-020.
rules.output: Both values recorded; the applied value flagged as (1) with the disagreement logged when they conflict.
rules.citation: §10.A.1 'Also not linked to anything'; §10.F.2 item 14; §7.3(b) item 9; §9.G IM40; §9.E IM30

rules.name: Momentum is STRUCTURAL, not a candlestick measurement
rules.statement: Momentum must be evaluated as a structural property of the JOURNEY toward the selected liquidity or imbalance target — the quality of that journey. The engine is FORBIDDEN to define momentum by candle body size, ATR ratios, or a fixed number of impulsive candles. Impulse candles are EVIDENCE that raises confidence; they are not the definition. Structure and liquidity remain the primary drivers, and the evaluation must be dynamic rather than resting on a fixed ATR ratio.
rules.inputs: The selected target and its state; the structure-writing record (chain of BOS/MSB toward the target); the imbalance inventory with fill/mitigation state; the liquidity-point spacing along the leg. NOT: ATR, absolute candle body size, impulse-candle counts as thresholds.
rules.output: A conformance assertion plus the structural evidence set that momentum was read from.
rules.citation: §2 D1 [R] and §2 D3 [R] (PDF Q5, pp.7–9, 12: 'momentum is a structural concept that evaluates the quality of the journey toward the selected liquidity or imbalance target'); §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER (ATR rejected as an input class in Q1 and Q5)

rules.name: Forward momentum confirmation detector (D4's three signs)
rules.statement: Detect and record the three forward-momentum confirmation signs toward a target: (1) momentum imbalances left unfilled behind the leg; (2) a large distance between liquidity points ('something pulls the price heavily'); (3) price still using its own imbalances to push — pullbacks bounce off their own gaps and produce the next break. Emit each as a boolean with the bar index and price coordinates of the evidence.
rules.inputs: Execution-TF and setup-TF candle series; the imbalance inventory with mitigation state; the swing/liquidity-point series with inter-point spacing; the break-event stream.
rules.output: momentum_confirm{sign1, sign2, sign3} each with evidence coordinates
rules.citation: §2 D4 (062_Momentum.md; echoed 023_Questionnaire.md 'the price is using its imbalances to reach the target'; 105); §9.C IM27 (Putting_in_all_together/1046)
rules.notes: How many of the three constitute 'momentum aligned' is not stated anywhere — see GRADE-031.

rules.name: Momentum slowdown / reversal detector (D5's four signs)
rules.statement: Detect and record the four momentum-slowdown signs, which fire AFTER target clearance: (1) the number of momentum imbalances reduces toward none and they get smaller; (2) the distance between liquidity points gets tighter and tighter; (3) imbalances fail their purpose one after another (no new BOS/MSB out of them); (4) a new momentum imbalance appears on the OPPOSITE side of the trend. Also detect the pre-hunt variant: a slowed trend building extra close-range liquidity right before the final sweep. Record which of the four fired, with coordinates.
rules.inputs: Post-clearance candle series on the setup TF; imbalance inventory with size and success/failure state per box; liquidity-point spacing series; the failed-imbalance-to-S/R-flip mutation detector.
rules.output: momentum_slowdown{sign1..sign4} each with evidence coordinates
rules.citation: §2 D5 (062_Momentum.md; 103_Examples.md; 023; 087_Examples.md); §9.D IM28 (Inefficiency_Main_Target_Bias/0692 — STRONG MOMENTUM vs SLOWED MOMENTUM panels); §2 C11 / §9.C IM25–IM26 (imbalance purpose failure and mutation to S/R)

rules.name: Forward → Reverse transition checklist (seven conditions)
rules.statement: Switching from Forward to Reverse requires MULTIPLE structural confirmations drawn from these seven: price slows down after reaching the destination; momentum begins deteriorating; momentum-imbalance failures appear; new momentum imbalances form in the opposite direction; failed imbalances become S/R flips; those new opposite-direction imbalances successfully hold price; a valid micro MSB confirms the new direction. All seven must be EVALUATED and recorded per decision, whatever quorum is later chosen. Reversal is judged by DECAY of the same momentum reading, not by a separate test: the question is not 'is momentum strong?' but 'has it deteriorated enough to justify a reversal?'.
rules.inputs: Target cleared-state; the outputs of GRADE-027 and GRADE-028; the S/R-flip mutation detector; the micro-MSB detector on the execution TF; the cool-off state from GRADE-035.
rules.output: reverse_conditions{c1..c7} + count_satisfied + the resulting mode ∈ {FORWARD, REVERSE}
rules.citation: §2 D5 [R] (PDF Q6, pp.14–15; PDF Q5, p.11); §1.3 [R]; §3.2 Part 1 step 6 Reverse branch (023_Questionnaire.md)
rules.notes: How many of the seven, and whether any (notably the micro MSB) is mandatory, is never stated. The workspace's cool-off prerequisite is NOT among the seven.

rules.name: Failure-safe direction — ambiguity resolves to FORWARD
rules.statement: When the structural confirmations of GRADE-029 are not present, the engine must assume the liquidity sweep was only part of the ongoing trend and CONTINUE evaluating Forward Trading. Ambiguity resolves to FORWARD, never to REVERSE — and this commonly occurs during bullet-train momentum. Separately: an MSB alone must never invalidate a higher-timeframe directional bias; only a complete structural reversal confirmed by the reverse-trading conditions may. Any counter-trend MSB while the HTF target is still valid immediately receives lower confidence.
rules.inputs: reverse_conditions from GRADE-029; the HTF target's validity state; the counter-trend break event, if any.
rules.output: mode = FORWARD by default; the reason code when a reversal is refused
rules.citation: §2 B3 [R] and §2 D5 [R] (PDF Q6, p.15); §2 A3 [R] Priority rule (PDF Q10, pp.23–24); §1.3 [R]

rules.name: No quorum threshold exists for any momentum aggregation
rules.statement: No source states how many of D4's three confirmation signs, how many of D5's four slowdown signs, or how many of Q6's seven transition conditions must be present, nor how much deterioration 'justifies a reversal' — there is no absolute level, no delta and no lookback window. The trader declined to fix these. The engine must expose them as declared, versioned parameters, report the chosen values and the observed counts in telemetry, and MUST NOT hard-code an undeclared quorum as if it were doctrine.
rules.inputs: n/a — specification-level blocker on GRADE-027, GRADE-028, GRADE-029.
rules.output: Declared parameter set {d4_quorum, d5_quorum, q6_quorum, deterioration_delta, lookback} each flagged as unratified.
rules.citation: §2 D5 [R] (PDF Q5, p.11 — 'Has the Momentum Score deteriorated enough to justify a reversal?'); §10.F.2 items 6 and 7
rules.triage_note: PARTIAL: the seven confirmations ship as a conjunction. Deterioration magnitude and lookback window stay open (trader Q).
rules.open_half_note: Ships the seven confirmations as a conjunction; deterioration magnitude and lookback stay unresolved (trader Q).

rules.name: BULLET TRAIN regime (the doctrinal definition)
rules.statement: BULLET TRAIN is the doctrinal name for incoming momentum that must not be faded: an uninterrupted chain of momentum candles making new momentum imbalances, fresh gaps punching through the concerning area, no deceleration and no counter micro-breaks. Operational consequences, all doctrinal: an i-MSB or a 1-minute MSB cannot stop it ('can you stop a train that is coming at you at 300Km/H with a i-MSB or 1Min MSB?'); reversing it requires a cooling/consolidation period and probably an HTF break (5Min or 15Min). Before fading, the engine must run and record the diagnostic checklist: is there a deeper concerning area? deeper liquidity? an unchecked timeframe? a missed institutional level or candlestick? an economic-data release? a global event? 'Momentum does not appear randomly, there is always something happening that you are missing.'
rules.inputs: Momentum-imbalance chain on the setup TF; gap penetration through the concerning area; presence/absence of counter micro-breaks; the deeper-objective scan across timeframes; the economic calendar and global-event feed.
rules.output: regime = BULLET_TRAIN + the diagnostic checklist result (which item, if any, explains it)
rules.citation: §2 D6 (023_Questionnaire.md, 062_Momentum.md, 104_Examples.md); §8 'Momentum picture'; §2 D6 [R] (it remains a live gate in three separate rulings)
rules.notes: The doctrine is intact and gates three separate decisions; only the invented machinery that would ASSIGN it is broken — see GRADE-033.

rules.name: DEFECT — the 'Bullet Train' score band 15–20 is arithmetically unreachable
rules.statement: The invented 8-component Momentum Score's top band '15–20 = Bullet Train' can never fire. Summing the printed per-component maxima (+3, +3, +3, +2, 0, +3, 0, 0) gives MAX = +14; the minima (0, 0, 0, 0, −2, 0, −4, −5) give MIN = −11; true reachable range is [−11, +14]. The single best market state the engine can ever observe scores 14 and is graded merely 'Strong' — short by 1 point to enter the band at all and by 6 points to reach its stated ceiling of 20. This breaks three separate rulings elsewhere in the same document that gate on the bullet-train state. Do NOT implement the band, and do NOT silently fix it: the source gives no basis to choose between adding 6 points to the positive components and re-cutting the bands against a +14 ceiling. The other bands (11–14 Strong, 7–10 Moderate, 3–6 Weak, ≤2 Exhausted) are contiguous and non-overlapping and ≤2 correctly absorbs the negative range. The NAME 'Bullet Train' is workspace doctrine and is unaffected — only the machinery that would assign it is broken.
rules.inputs: n/a — specification-level blocker.
rules.output: A conformance assertion: no bullet-train classification is derived from the score; the doctrinal detector GRADE-032 is used instead.
rules.citation: §10.D D-2 (PDF Q5, pp.8–11); §10.F.1 defect D1; §7.4 DEAD NUMBERS REGISTER; §2 D6 [R] warning
rules.triage_note: WITHDRAWN: same as GATE-034.

rules.name: The Momentum Score is invented machinery, not doctrine
rules.statement: The 8-component Momentum Score appears in no workspace page and in none of the 1,258 chart images, and has never been traded. It must never be cited as strategy, never be quoted to the trader as 'the method', and never be back-filled into the documentary sections. It additionally introduces a coupling nothing in the workspace makes: component 6 feeds the SAME three-grade structure-box scale that sets RISK % into a MOMENTUM number, and never says which box is meant. It also has no news/macro component, although the doctrine makes economic-data days and global events the PRIMARY diagnostic when a bullet train runs through a concerning area. If a score is built at all it must be labelled engine machinery in telemetry and kept strictly separable from the documented qualitative regime.
rules.inputs: n/a — a provenance and labelling rule.
rules.output: Any score emitted must carry authority_class = ENGINE_DESIGN, never STRATEGY.
rules.citation: §10 STANDING RULE; §10.D D-1 and its component-6 note; §10.F.2 item 9; §2 D3 [R] ('the Momentum Score the quote names is a [D] engine object… this line is not evidence that the strategy contains a score')
rules.triage_note: Retained as the standing provenance prohibition: any momentum score must carry authority_class = ENGINE_DESIGN and must never be quoted as the trader's doctrine.

rules.name: Cool-off period is a hard prerequisite for reversal
rules.statement: A liquidity sweep alone never authorises a reversal: a cool-off — a slowdown in momentum, consolidation, a range — is a prerequisite. 'Still after the sweep, it has no intention to reverse, there's no failing imbalance or structure shift, it needs a cool off period, a slow down in momentum before considering a reversal.' Documented durations, which the rulings OMIT rather than retire and which therefore stand unopposed: 'the momentum slowdown takes around 2 days before the reversal' and 'it takes around 24H to cool off until it totally loses its momentum, then the price shifts at 9:30AM in the morning the next day'. The rulings reduce cool-off to the qualitative 'price slows down after reaching the destination' and drop it from both the transition-condition list and the score.
rules.inputs: Time and price action since the sweep; the consolidation/overlap detector; the absence of fresh old-direction gaps; the NY 9:30 open marker.
rules.output: cool_off{satisfied: bool, elapsed_duration, consolidation_evidence}
rules.citation: §2 D7 (100_Examples.md, 104_Examples.md, 062_Momentum.md) and its 'Omission to carry' warning; §1.3 step 3; §10.F.2 item 8
rules.notes: No minimum duration or consolidation criterion is ruled. The two workspace durations are observations from worked examples, not a stated threshold — do not harden them into a rule without a ruling.
rules.triage_note: CALIBRATED (weak, n=3): duration ships as DECLARED, UNRATIFIED CONFIG (24H / ~2 days), not as a fitted value. Recommend config over fitting at this n.

rules.name: Prefer trading with slow momentum, stand aside against strong momentum
rules.statement: Prefer setups where momentum into the target has already slowed; a deviation is a flag, not a failure. 'Taking a trade against such a momentum is quite dangerous because we do not know how much the price can go further, instead trading a setup with a slow momentum is so much easier and smooth because the price was already cooling off.' The slowed phase supplies BOTH the entry permission and the destination list: the accumulated LIQ pools left behind by the decaying leg become the targets ('Slowed Momentum IMB much easier TARGETS'). Picture test: shrinking candle bodies/ranges at a target zone = tradable; giant candles into the zone = stand aside.
rules.inputs: regime from GRADE-039; candle range/body trend into the target zone; the LIQ-ray inventory accumulated over the decaying leg.
rules.output: preference_flag ∈ {ALIGNED, DEVIATION} + the reason
rules.citation: §2 D8 (061_Inefficiency_Main_Target_Bias.md); §9.D IM28 (Inefficiency_Main_Target_Bias/0692 — 'Trading against a very strong momentum is dangerous. Let the price reach its destination and slow down!')

rules.name: Strong Trend vs Strong Trend + Momentum (the unmitigated discriminator)
rules.statement: Two-tier trend grader with a crisp printed test. STRONG TREND = the trend is powered by imbalances (its pullbacks consume imbalances and produce the next break): 'If the TREND is powered by IMBALANCE, we call it a STRONG TREND'. STRONG TREND + MOMENTUM = the trend uses imbalances AND leaves UNMITIGATED imbalances behind: 'If the TREND uses IMBALANCE, but also leaves UNMITIGATED IMBALANCES we call it a STRONG TREND + MOMENTUM'. The discriminator is therefore mitigation state, not candle size: on one leg, count the IMB boxes that were retested versus the Momentum IMB boxes that never were. The word 'unmitigated' appears nowhere in the workspace text — this two-tier formula exists only on the image.
rules.inputs: The break-event chain of the leg; the imbalance inventory on that leg with per-box mitigation state (retested vs untouched).
rules.output: trend_tier ∈ {NONE, STRONG_TREND, STRONG_TREND_PLUS_MOMENTUM} + the mitigated / unmitigated box counts
rules.citation: §9.C IM27 (Putting_in_all_together/1046 — the 'Trend + Momentum' card); §2 D9 (060_Inefficiency_Basics.md); §2 C6 (062_Momentum.md)
rules.notes: RECONSTRUCTED — the extracted-rule payload handed to this contract was truncated mid-statement at this ID. Text restored from §9.C IM27 and §2 D9/C6; the ID is preserved so downstream references do not churn. Verify against IM27 before shipping.

rules.name: Imbalance purpose test and the permanent-trend-change rule
rules.statement: Pass/fail test on every imbalance: 'IMBALANCE PURPOSE — We expect imbalances to push the price to make NEW BoS or MSB' toward the main target bias. Fail state is annotated 'No BoS? Purpose Failed'. Location decides meaning: a failure BEFORE the target is a temporary detour (the inducement); a failure AFTER the target is cleared gets its own named rule — 'PERMANENT TREND CHANGE — If the IMBALANCE fails After clearing the MAIN TARGET, It is most likely to change the trend for good.' Failed imbalances then MUTATE: 'FAILED IMBALANCES can turn into Support or Resistance areas! Extra confluence!' The engine must record, per imbalance, its purpose verdict, whether the main target was cleared at the time, and whether the failed box later held price from the other side.
rules.inputs: Imbalance inventory with per-box outcome (produced a new BOS/MSB or not); main-target cleared-state at the time of the failure; subsequent retests of the failed box from the opposite side.
rules.output: per-imbalance {purpose: PASS|FAIL, target_cleared_at_failure: bool, mutated_to_sr_flip: bool}
rules.citation: §9.C IM25 (Putting_in_all_together/1048, 1046, 1051 — the purpose card and the 'PERMENANT TREND CHANGE' [sic] rule); §9.C IM26 (1050, 1051 — 'MUTATION of FAILED IMBALANCE'); §2 C10 and §2 C11 (060_Inefficiency_Basics.md, 023, 098_Examples.md, 103_Examples.md)
rules.notes: RECONSTRUCTED to close the reference chain broken by the truncated input payload. The permanence claim is IMAGE-ONLY — §2 C10's text says only 'a possible trend change'. Do not harden 'for good' into an irreversible engine state.

rules.name: Qualitative momentum regime classifier (the implementable substitute for the broken score)
rules.statement: Emit a qualitative momentum regime, never a numeric band, until GRADE-033 is ruled. STRONG_MOMENTUM: a staircase of Momentum IMB boxes each leaving a LIQ ray behind, wide swing spacing, imbalances still producing breaks — 'Trading against a very strong momentum is dangerous. Let the price reach its destination and slow down!'. SLOWED_MOMENTUM: decaying arc, tightening swing spacing, shrinking/failing imbalances, accumulated LIQ pools — 'SLOWED MOMENTUM — HIGHER amount of LIQUIDITY (Much easier to trade)'. BULLET_TRAIN (GRADE-032): an uninterrupted chain punching through the concerning area with no deceleration and no counter micro-breaks. The regime is derived from GRADE-027 / GRADE-028 / GRADE-032 / GRADE-037 evidence sets only, from structural facts, never from ATR or candle size (GRADE-026), and the quorum used to pick the regime is a declared parameter, not doctrine (GRADE-031).
rules.inputs: momentum_confirm (GRADE-027); momentum_slowdown (GRADE-028); bullet-train evidence (GRADE-032); trend_tier (GRADE-037).
rules.output: regime ∈ {BULLET_TRAIN, STRONG_MOMENTUM, SLOWED_MOMENTUM, UNCLEAR} + the evidence set and the quorum applied
rules.citation: §9.D IM28 (Inefficiency_Main_Target_Bias/0692 — the paired STRONG MOMENTUM / SLOWED MOMENTUM panels); §2 D4, D5, D6, D8; §8 'Momentum picture'; §10.D D-2 (why no numeric band may be emitted)
rules.notes: RECONSTRUCTED to close the reference chain broken by the truncated input payload (GRADE-036 consumes 'regime from GRADE-039'). Status OPEN because the regime boundary between STRONG_MOMENTUM and BULLET_TRAIN is nowhere quantified and the only machinery the corpus offers for it is the broken score.
rules.triage_note: CRITIC DEMOTION: stays OPEN. The promotion rested on a definition-by-negation; the actual open question (the bullet-train boundary) is conceded TRADER_ONLY elsewhere in the same document.

rules.name: Concerning liquidity is the next unresolved objective, NOT the closest
rules.statement: OVERRIDE. “The concerning liquidity is therefore not simply the closest liquidity. It is the next unresolved objective that supports the active institutional destination”; “Distance alone never determines the destination”. The concept “is not determined by a fixed distance, percentage, or ATR threshold”; the engine “should not ask: 'Is liquidity within X% or Y × ATR?'”. Proximity survives ONLY as an ordering input among same-direction, same-timeframe candidates. The workspace's own “we are only concerned about the closest swing point” (059), 085's “closest not hunted deep swing liquidity”, §9.B IM10's printed CONCERNING METHOD → CLOSEST LIQUIDITY POINT formula and 0613's three-state distance grading are all superseded as the SELECTION RULE and survive only as inputs.
rules.inputs: Liquidity and imbalance inventories across the analysis timeframes; the active institutional destination; the cleared/uncleared state of each objective.
rules.output: concerning_objective{id, price, tf, type, why_selected} — the 'why' must name the institutional destination it supports, not a distance.

rules.name: The three-step target-selection procedure (and its six defects)
rules.statement: Step 1 Strategic Target Selection — “The engine must first execute the higher-level strategic analysis described in the strategy before determining which liquidity or imbalance is currently relevant”, over twelve named inputs including the hierarchy Monthly → Weekly → Daily → 4H → 2H → 1H.
