rules.name: Doctrine-vs-practice gap on realised R
rules.statement: Three different R levels coexist in the corpus and the learning loop must keep them apart rather than averaging them: the RULED preference is ≈3R with a 2R floor (GATE-025); the teaching deck DRAWS ≈2.9R wherever a bracket is illustrative (GATE-046); and the trader's own realised executions in the corpus run 1.4–1.7R — “the cards sell ~2.7–2.9R and the worked examples realise 1.4–1.7R”. The 70%-at-2R partial mechanically caps most realised R near 2R by construction. Record planned_rr, drawn/reference rr where applicable, and realised_rr as three distinct fields.
rules.inputs: planned RR at entry; realised RR at close.
rules.output: planned_rr, realised_rr, rr_gap (telemetry).
rules.citation: §8 measurement discipline; §9 IM30; §9.J IM114; §2 H5 [R]; §10.C reward rows

rules.name: R system and the VIRTUAL account base
rules.statement: Risk is expressed in R against a VIRTUAL account size, not against the broker balance. “Think you have a 1.000$ account… we mostly call it 100R, basically 100 risk, so basically if i risk 1% of my account i would be risking 10$ this is what we call 1R… If my risk reward ratio is 1:2 it means i am expecting to win 2R equals to 20$.” The virtual base is deliberately smaller than the broker balance: “i have 20.000$ in my broker account but i want my account to act as 1.000$ and risk 10$ per each trade”; “this number here does not matter, it is the actual cash in the broker account… what matters is the number i set here in the settings of risk reward tool”. Telemetry must record BOTH the virtual account size used for sizing and the actual balance, or risk-% conformance cannot be checked.
rules.inputs: virtual_account_size (configured); risk_pct from GATE-032; stop distance.
rules.output: risk_amount = virtual_account_size × risk_pct; 1R = risk_amount.
rules.citation: §2 H4 (074_Risk_Management_Basics.md); §2 H10 (074, 114_Examples.md)

rules.name: Position size is scaled purely by the quantity field
rules.statement: Risk is set by the QUANTITY, computed from the RR tool: “this Qty label which is quantity is the most important thing of this tool, determines the contract number you will use in your broker”; “the quantity needed was 0.03… 0.03/2 becomes 0.015… magically my risk dropped to 0.5% of the 1000$ which is 5$ basically 0.5R… before typing your quantity you can easily decide your risk”. “All these four numbers came from the risk reward tool” — entry, quantity, SL, TP. Therefore: quantity = risk_amount / |entry − stop| (per contract/unit), and the recorded quantity must reproduce the recorded risk_pct to within rounding. This is the single arithmetic identity that makes risk conformance checkable from telemetry alone.
rules.inputs: risk_amount (SIZE-001); entry price; selected stop price; instrument contract specification.
rules.output: quantity + the identity check quantity × |entry − stop| ≈ virtual_account_size × risk_pct.
rules.citation: §2 H4 (054_Execution_on_Broker.md, 120_Execution_on_Broker.md); §2 H10 (074, 114); §3.7 step 6

rules.name: Leverage is neutral to risk
rules.statement: “Using different leverage has zero effect on the money i will win or lose, it only changed the cost of opening the position that's it”; “It is all about capital needed”. Caveat with a real failure mode: crypto brokers liquidate at ≈ −80% PnL on ISOLATED margin, so a 100X isolated position “can be liquidated before reaching the actual SL” — i.e. leverage does not change intended risk but can change REALISED risk by pre-empting the stop. The engine must record leverage and margin mode so a liquidation can be distinguished from a stop-out in the outcome data.
rules.inputs: leverage; margin mode (isolated/cross); position notional.
rules.output: telemetry leverage, margin_mode; exit_reason must distinguish STOP_HIT from LIQUIDATION.
rules.citation: §2 H11 (074_Risk_Management_Basics.md, 114_Examples.md)

rules.name: The 2% tier is unreachable and was retired by omission
rules.statement: H2's ceiling — “You shall never risk more than 2% of your account in any trade… if you are risking like 2% of the account it should be the most magical setup” — and §9.G IM40's printed pairing “2% = 2R reserved for a 4R Perfect setup” both become UNREACHABLE cells once the matrix caps at 1.50%. Neither is retracted as doctrine and neither is explained away: the ruling simply never mentions 2%. Independent corroboration that capping is the safer reading: across the whole image corpus the 2% tier is never demonstrated with money anywhere — every execution frame uses 1% = 1R. Consequence for the engine: risk_pct > 0.015 is a HARD violation, and the fact that the retirement was by omission rather than argument must stay visible in the open-questions register.
rules.inputs: risk_pct emitted by the sizer.
rules.output: conformance assertion risk_pct ≤ 0.015 and risk_pct ∈ the nine matrix values.
rules.citation: §2 H2 [O]; §10.A.1 'What this kills'; §10.B O3; §9.G IM40 (PDF Q9 p.21; Q14 p.29)

rules.name: Swing points, strong/weak highs and lows
rules.statement: Detect the swing-point series per timeframe; these are the atoms of the whole system — “Liquidity starts with swing points like swing highs and swing lows where the stop losses are placed”. Classify each: “Every single time a new break of structure happens in the trend direction, we just create a strong low and a possible weak high… When the buyers push the price and take out a weak high, a strong low is confirmed”, mirrored for downtrends. Box shortcut: “the highest point in the box will be your strong high”. Swings carry per-timeframe identity — “every single TF will have their own strong highs and lows” — and a swing that is strong on several TFs at once is a COMBO strong swing and is repeatedly defended. Every detected swing must be emitted with its price, bar, timeframe and strong/weak classification, because every liquidity level, structure box and stop anchor downstream is derived from one.
rules.inputs: Candle series per timeframe.
rules.output: swings[] {id, tf, bar, price, kind ∈ {HIGH, LOW}, strength ∈ {STRONG, WEAK, UNCONFIRMED}, combo_tfs[]}
rules.citation: §1.1 (058_Liquidity_Basics.md); §2 A5 (055_Structure_Basics.md, 056, 105); §2 A6 (055); §2 A7 (080_Examples.md)

rules.name: Imbalance inventory with fill state
rules.statement: Detect all four named inefficiency types and carry each with its fill state. Types: fair value gap (“classic imbalances”); volume imbalance (“the empty space between candle bodies with only wicks”); gap (“the large voids between candlesticks… gaps and volume imbalances are the same thing the only difference is the wicks”); BPR — the boxed OVERLAP of a minimum of two opposite-direction imbalances, extended right, with ≥3 overlapping gaps = SUPER BPR. Fill states, fixed by the images: half filled / fully filled / fully filled and violated / first-vs-second test; an imbalance “stays extremely reactive until it is fully filled”. Also carry MOMENTUM imbalances — the large gaps left behind by impulsive moves and never filled — separately, since they are simultaneously a momentum signal, an inner target after the switch, and stop anchor #2.
rules.inputs: Candle series per timeframe.
rules.output: imbalances[] {id, tf, bar_range, price_band, type ∈ {FVG, VOLUME, GAP, BPR, SUPER_BPR}, is_momentum: bool, fill_state, test_count}
rules.citation: §2 C1–C6 (060_Inefficiency_Basics.md, 062_Momentum.md, 068, 105); §9.J IM61 (the four fill states), IM62, IM64, IM66; §2 L2 (033_Technical_Indicators.md — the two indicators run in parallel)

rules.name: Liquidity-pool inventory (six classes, taken/untaken state)
rules.statement: Detect and carry, each with a taken/untaken flag and a timeframe tag: (1) swing-point levels; (2) equal highs/lows — perfect and relative, per TARGET-006, often hidden on HTF and revealed on LTF; (3) parabolic / compressed liquidity — “compact trends in LTFs, these areas will be very tight”, used “a 100% exactly the same way with equals”; (4) institutional levels — monthly / weekly / daily deep-V swing extremes; (5) institutional candlesticks — PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, PMH/PML and the Monday range, each with high, low and EQ midline; (6) session levels — Asia and London range highs/lows, and their EQ as a reverse-trade target. Also carry DIAGONAL pools: the range/three-tap charts use an unnumbered LIQ (also Lq, LQ) for trendline pools along a staircase, a different geometry from the horizontal LIQ1…LIQ9 labels. Only “fresh not hunted liquidity levels” count as objectives.
rules.inputs: Candle series across the analysis and execution timeframes; session and calendar boundaries in NY time.
rules.output: liquidity_pools[] {id, tf, class, price (or the two endpoints for a diagonal), state ∈ {UNTESTED, TESTED_NOT_CONSUMED, CONSUMED}, boosters[]}

rules.name: Sweep events
rules.statement: Emit a sweep event whenever price runs through a marked pool: the excursion beyond the level with its penetration measured, plus the post-sweep reaction that TARGET-005 requires before the pool may be called consumed. Carry the three documented degradations: (a) LIQUIDITY SWEEP FAIL — approach to within a hair of the level with the wick never crossing it (“price comes extremely close to the LIQ1 point but it was never hunted”); (b) TINY-WICK INSUFFICIENCY — “Do you think the one day liquidity point can be hunted with this very very tiny wick? Not so much”, now calibrated at ≤~1% = weak, expect a second run; (c) DEGRADED SWEEP — a prior breakout/new highs beyond the level before the final poke (“this is not the ideal sweep, it has BO and new highs over level before sweep”). Also emit ENGINEERED-LIQUIDITY build: a cluster of small, closely spaced swings forming beside a concerning level with shrinking candles just before the thrust.
rules.inputs: Liquidity pools from PRIM-003; candle series; prior closes beyond the level.
rules.output: sweeps[] {id, pool_id, bar, penetration_abs, penetration_pct, wick_or_close, degraded: bool, failed: bool, reaction_evidence}

rules.name: Break events — MSB vs BOS discriminated by geometry, never by expansion
rules.statement: Emit break events with the swing each break consumed and the leg direction. Discriminator, from the images: SAME candle quality, DIFFERENT location — an MSB breaks the last swing AGAINST the trend; a BOS breaks the prior swing WITH it. Do NOT disambiguate by acronym expansion: MSB now expands to “Market Structure Break” and BOS is glossed “break of structure”, so the two expansions have collapsed and only the geometry separates them. Carry the scale variants: main MSB (HTF), i-MSB / internal MSB (substructure, the entry and stop-anchor object), micro MSB (the reversal-feasibility trigger), and the fake-MSB classification of GRADE-008. OCR note: the workspace's own prose twice transposes MSB to “MBS” — map MBS→MSB, do not treat it as a new token. And NEVER abbreviate “Manipulated Structure Box” to MSB.
rules.inputs: Swing series from PRIM-001; candle series; the prevailing leg direction.
rules.output: breaks[] {id, tf, bar, type ∈ {MSB, BOS}, scale ∈ {MAIN, INTERNAL, MICRO}, consumed_swing_id, valid (ENTRY-003), fake_msb (GRADE-008)}
rules.citation: §2 A2, §2 A3 (055_Structure_Basics.md, 052, 062, 084, 098, 105); §6 glossary MSB/BOS/MBS rows; §9.J IM81 (the geometric discriminator); §7.3(b) items 11 and 12

rules.name: S/R flip zones are ZONES, never lines
rules.statement: A support/resistance flip is a level or zone broken one way then retested from the other side and holding — break → retest → go. The images are explicit that these are ZONES, not thin lines, and that a stop placed at a flip zone must cover the WHOLE zone. Two mechanisms feed the inventory: failed imbalances that “mutate to resistance and support areas that can hold the price in the future just like regular S/R flips” (GRADE-038), and the reactive-level test — “draw a ligne, single line around your possible entry point… check if there are a lot of reactions to that price level… it can easily act as S/R flip level”. Flips are also one of the three amplifier classes (GATE-038), so the same object appears in two roles and must carry both.
rules.inputs: Broken levels with subsequent opposite-side retests; the failed-imbalance stream; touch counts per price band.
rules.output: sr_flips[] {id, tf, price_band (never a single price), origin ∈ {FAILED_IMBALANCE, BROKEN_LEVEL}, touch_count, quality_factors}
rules.citation: §2 A15 (060_Inefficiency_Basics.md, 023, 067_Magic_Amplifiers.md, 112_Examples.md); §2 C11; §9.J IM76 (zones-not-lines), IM77 (three quality factors), IM78, IM79 (stop covers the whole zone); §9.J IM69 (Breaker Block = failed Order Block ≡ an S/R flip)
